title: [PR] fix(asyncio): Is_Cluster gives the sync probe a sync Retry
description: Fixes #299. `Is_Cluster` builds a synchronous `redis.Redis` probe from the async pool's `connection_kwargs`. When the async client is created with `retry=`, those kwargs hold a `redis.asyncio.retry.Retry`; the synchronous probe called its coroutine `call_with_retry` without awaiting it and crashed with `TypeError: argument of type 'coroutine' is not iterable`. So no `retry` value worked with the async client. The probe now gets a `redis.retry.Retry` with the same backoff, retry count and supported errors, which are the fields redis-py's `AbstractRetry` itself hashes on. This follows the approach of #235 (translate the async pool's kwargs into what the synchronous constructor accepts). `types-redis` predates `AbstractRetry`, hence the narrow `type: ignore[attr-defined]`. ### Tests - `test_is_cluster_does_not_crash_on_an_async_retry_policy`: against an absent server the probe fails with a connection error, never a `TypeError` (fails on `main`). - `test_async_client_accepts_an_async_retry_policy`: `FalkorDB(retry=...)` runs a query end to end (fails on `main`). Full suite: 108 passed, 2 xpassed against `falkordb/falkordb:v4.18.3`; `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy falkordb/` clean. `pyspelling` was not available locally. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #299. `Is_Cluster` builds a synchronous `redis.Redis` probe from the async pool's `connection_kwargs`, and when the async client was created with `retry=`, those kwargs held an async `Retry` whose `call_with_retry` is a coroutine that the sync probe never awaited. The probe now receives a synchronous `redis.retry.Retry` with the same backoff, retry count, and supported errors, so `retry=` works end to end with the async client. Written for commit e48adcb496d78e4f6e65e03e5e202f6111a4a91c. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed an error that could occur when using asynchronous retry policies with cluster detection. * FalkorDB clients configured with asynchronous retry policies can now run queries and close cleanly.

title: [Issue] asyncio: Is_Cluster crashes when the client is given a retry policy
description:
### What happens

Passing the documented `retry=` argument to the async client fails before any query runs:

```python
from falkordb.asyncio import FalkorDB
from redis.asyncio.retry import Retry
from redis.backoff import NoBackoff

FalkorDB(host="localhost", port=6379, retry=Retry(NoBackoff(), 0))
```

```
falkordb/asyncio/cluster.py, in Is_Cluster
    return "redis_mode" in info and info["redis_mode"] == "cluster"
TypeError: argument of type 'coroutine' is not iterable
RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'Retry.call_with_retry' was never awaited
```

### Why

`Is_Cluster` builds a synchronous `redis.Redis` probe from the async pool's `connection_kwargs`. When the caller passed `retry=`, those kwargs hold a `redis.asyncio.retry.Retry`, whose `call_with_retry` is a coroutine. The synchronous probe calls it and never awaits it, so `info()` returns a coroutine.

Passing a synchronous `redis.retry.Retry` instead does not help either: the probe then works, but the async connections get a retry object whose `call_with_retry` is not awaitable. So there is currently no `retry` value that works with the async client, even though the async client is the only way to keep the documented `socket_timeout` plus a bounded retry policy. (redis-py's default retries the connect step 10 times with exponential backoff; against an unreachable server with `socket_timeout=1` we measured 11 attempts over ~15 s.)

### Versions

falkordb 1.7.1 (also current `main`), redis 8.1.0, Python 3.12.

A fix in the same style as #235 (translate the async pool's kwargs into what the synchronous probe accepts) follows in a PR.

title: [PR] fix(schema): refresh GraphSchema cache on query execution to prevent stale property key mappings (#243)
description:
Fixes #243

### Problem
When a graph is deleted externally (e.g. raw `GRAPH.DELETE`, process crash, or another client worker) without calling `Graph.delete()` on a Python `Graph` instance, `GraphSchema` retains stale property key mappings from the old graph. If a new graph is created under the same name with a different property key registration order, `RETURN n` (compact format) silently maps property IDs to incorrect property names, returning corrupted data.

### Solution
1. **Independent Dirty Tracking**: Added `_dirty_labels`, `_dirty_properties`, and `_dirty_relations` flags to `GraphSchema` (sync & async).
2. **Query Execution Marking**: Set dirty flags on query execution in `Graph._query` and `AsyncGraph._query`.
3. **On-Demand Cache Refresh**: Updated `get_property()`, `get_label()`, and `get_relation()` to automatically fetch up-to-date schema metadata (`DB.PROPERTYKEYS`) on demand when dirty.
4. **Regression Tests**: Added unit tests `test_schema_cache_on_external_delete` in `tests/test_graph.py` and `test_async_schema_cache_on_external_delete` in `tests/test_async_graph.py`.

### Verification
Ran regression test suite. `RETURN n` and `RETURN properties(n)` now match 100%. All pre-commit checks (`ruff format`, `ruff check`, `mypy falkordb/`) passed cleanly.

title: [PR] ci: alert on a cancelled scheduled run, not just a failed one
description:
The daily `edge` run is our early warning for engine changes, but the alert
that reports it never fires when the run hangs.

`report-scheduled-failure` is gated on:

```yaml
if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'schedule' && contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') }}
```

A job stopped by a timeout, or by GitHub's six hour ceiling, reports
`cancelled`, not `failure`. So the alert is skipped in exactly the case it
exists for. This adds `cancelled` to the condition.

It also caps the job at `timeout-minutes: 30`. Recent nightlies finish in
about two minutes, so anything near the cap is stuck, and failing at 30
minutes reports a result the same morning instead of holding a runner until
the six hour ceiling.

The `github.event_name == 'schedule'` guard stays, so a force push that
cancels an in flight PR run still does not raise an alert.

title: [Issue] Async FalkorDB client is unusable with recent redis-py versions
[PR] fix: security hardening, correctness fixes and modernization
description:
## Summary

A review of the client surfaced a set of verified correctness and security
bugs, plus some gaps against current Python packaging practice. This PR fixes
them and adds regression coverage.

It also repairs the Test workflow, which was **already failing on `main`**
before these changes: `falkordb/falkordb:edge` no longer emits the `Results`
root operation in `GRAPH.EXPLAIN` / `GRAPH.PROFILE` output and renamed `Join`
to `Union`, breaking 15 tests that asserted on exact plan text.

> [!WARNING]
> **Breaking change:** `ssl_check_hostname` now defaults to `True`. TLS users
> whose certificate CN/SAN does not match the host they connect to must pass
> `ssl_check_hostname=False` explicitly. This matches the redis-py 7.x default.

## Changes

### Security

- **Cypher injection via parameters.** `stringify_param_value()` fell back to
  `str()` for unrecognized types, so a value whose `__str__` returned Cypher was
  spliced verbatim into the query header. Verified live: a crafted object
  rendering as `1 CREATE (:PWNED) //` actually created a node. Replaced the
  fallback with a strict type whitelist that raises `TypeError`.
- **Remote denial of service via NUL byte.** `graph.query("RETURN $p", {"p": "a\x00b"})`
  succeeded, then the server died seconds later with a Rust `NulError` panic
  (`CString::new(...).unwrap()`) in its background telemetry thread; the panic
  payload decoded to exactly the client-generated header. `quote_string()` now
  rejects NUL with `ValueError`. This needs a server-side fix too — the client
  change only stops this client from triggering it, and I'll open an issue upstream.
- **Credential stripping.** Cluster detection mutated the live pool's
  `connection_kwargs` in place, removing credentials from every subsequent
  connection made from that pool. Now copies the dict.
- **TLS downgrade in `from_url()`.** A `rediss://` URL produced a client that
  reconnected *without* TLS, because `ssl` was never derived from the parsed
  pool.
- **TLS hostname verification** is on by default (see warning above).

### Correctness

- `AsyncGraph` dropped the coroutine from `schema.refresh()` instead of awaiting
  it, so recovery from `SchemaVersionMismatchException` never refreshed the
  schema and the retry re-read a stale cache.
- `call_procedure()` appended to the caller's `args` list, corrupting it on reuse.
- `parse_scalar()` indexed its dispatch table with an unvalidated, server-supplied
  type id — a new scalar type raised `IndexError`. Now falls back to the
  unknown-type parser and reports via `warnings.warn` instead of `sys.stderr`.
- `ExecutionPlan` measured indentation from whole-line length rather than leading
  spaces, so any change in operation-name width shifted the parsed tree. Also
  fixed empty plans, an unguarded `None` regex match, dead code after `return []`,
  and `assert` used for input validation (which vanishes under `python -O`).
- `Path.__str__` compared an `Edge.src_node` (a `Node`) against an int node

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
### Follow-up backlog (not addressed here)

The review turned up a few sync/async parity gaps that are larger than this PR
and are better handled separately:

- **No async sentinel support.** There is no `falkordb/asyncio/sentinel.py`, so
  an `AsyncFalkorDB` pointed at a sentinel silently talks to the *sentinel*
  rather than the master. This one is arguably a bug rather than a gap.
- **`AsyncFalkorDB.__init__` is missing 8 parameters** the sync client accepts
  (`dynamic_startup_nodes`, `url`, `ssl_ca_path`, `ssl_password`,
  `ssl_validate_ocsp`, …).
- **`Is_Cluster` does blocking network I/O during async construction**, stalling
  the event loop. Fixing it properly needs lazy or async detection, i.e. an API
  change.
- **The async client class is named `FalkorDB`, not `AsyncFalkorDB`**, contrary
  to what `AGENTS.md` described. I corrected the docs to match the code here,
  but the rename may be the better long-term call.
- **`AsyncQueryResult` exposes mutable `header`/`result_set`/`graph` attributes**
  where the sync side uses read-only properties.
- **`Path.nodes()`/`edges()` are methods, not properties**, inconsistent with the
  rest of the models; left alone to avoid breaking the existing API.

Happy to open issues for any of these.

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
Merged `main` (resolving the conflicts) and worked through the review. Thanks — two of these were real gaps in the hardening this PR set out to do.

### Fixed

**Reject NUL bytes in every Cypher identifier key** (`graph.py`, `helpers.py`) — correct, and the more important of the two. NUL was rejected in parameter *values* but not in parameter names or nested map keys, both of which are interpolated into the header between backticks:

```python
>>> Graph._build_params_header(g, {"a\x00b": 1})
'CYPHER `a\x00b`=1 '     # same header NUL that crashes the server
```

The three identifier checks (non-empty, no backtick, no NUL) were duplicated across the two files, so they are now one `quote_identifier()` helper used by both. Covered for top-level names, nested map keys and `bytes` keys.

**Make `__hash__` consistent with `__eq__`** (`node.py`, `edge.py`) — correct, and both were constructible:

```python
Node(node_id=1, labels="A") == Node(labels="A")   # True, hashes differed
len({with_id, without_id})                        # 2
```

Hashes now use only what equality always compares — labels for `Node`, relation for `Edge` — so the id, which equality deliberately tolerates being unset, no longer participates. `Edge.__eq__` short-circuited on a matching id alone, which left *no* invariant to hash on, so it now also requires the relation to match; two edges with the same id but different relationship types don't describe the same edge. Verified exhaustively over every id/label/relation/property combination (288 pairs, 0 violations), and `Path` inherits the fix.

**Do not include raw query values in warnings** (`query_result.py` ×2) — agreed, the message now identifies the scalar *type id* instead of echoing the value.

**Use of the return value of a procedure** (CodeQL, `query_result.py`) — made the unknown-scalar fallback an explicit branch rather than selecting `__parse_unknown` as a value parser.

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
## Second review round — 3 fixed, 1 corrected on the facts

### Fixed

**`helpers.py` — `Decimal` coerced through `float()`** — valid, and worse than reported. Two distinct bugs:

```
Decimal("1.2345678901234567890123")  ->  1.2345678901234567     # digits dropped
Decimal("1E+400")                    ->  ValueError "NaN and Infinity"
```

The second is the serious one: `1E+400` is a perfectly finite `Decimal`, but `float()` overflows it to `inf` and trips the non-finite guard, so the client rejected a value it should have passed on. `Decimal` now has its own branch using `Decimal.is_finite()` and renders from `str(value)`.

Cypher has no arbitrary-precision decimal type, so a `Decimal` always narrows to a double *somewhere*. The point is that the client should not add a second, silent rounding, and should not invent an error. Verified against the live server:

| input | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `Decimal("0.1")` | `0.1` | `0.1` |
| `Decimal("1.2345678901234567890123")` | rounded client-side, then again server-side | server narrows once, returns `1.23456789012346` |
| `Decimal("1E+400")` | client-side `ValueError` claiming Infinity | server: `Failed to parse the value of parameter 'v'` |
| `Decimal("NaN")` / `Decimal("Infinity")` | rejected | still rejected — no Cypher literal exists |

**`AGENTS.md:71`** — correct, and my own drift: I deleted `tests/plan_utils.py` when merging `main` in favour of its `plan_helpers.py`, and did not update the file listing. Fixed.

**`graph.py:628` / `graph.py:654`** — fixed, though not for the stated reason. See below.

### Corrected

The report says suppressing `ResponseError` means "connection failures or permission errors get silently ignored". That isn't so — in redis-py these are separate branches of the hierarchy:

```
AuthenticationError -> ConnectionError -> RedisError     # not a ResponseError
ResponseError       -> RedisError
```

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
## Conflicts resolved, plus a review that found the hardening was incomplete

### Conflicts

`main` had landed #276 (async connection-pool kwargs), release 1.7.1 and the redis 8.x pin. Three files conflicted, both sides having fixed the same things independently:

- **`cluster.py` / `asyncio/cluster.py`** — both branches derived the same "don't pop from the live pool dict" fix. Took main's `.copy()` idiom and kept the comment explaining why it matters.
- **`asyncio/graph.py`** — main annotated the instance (`self.schema: GraphSchema = GraphSchema(self)  # type: ignore[assignment]`). This branch already declares `schema: AsyncGraphSchema` at class level, which types *every read* of `self.schema` rather than only the assignment, so main's annotation and its ignore were redundant. Confirmed with `reveal_type` that mypy still resolves the async schema, and mypy is clean without the ignore.

### Review

I had the branch reviewed adversarially against a live server. It found **six real bugs, four of them in my own hardening**, which is the uncomfortable but useful outcome. All are fixed.

**One mistake, made four times.** `isinstance()` accepts subclasses, so any security decision made by *calling a method on the untrusted value* is caller-overridable:

| Where | How it broke |
|---|---|
| `int`/`float`/`Decimal` | `repr(value)` on a subclass — `EvilInt.__repr__` returned `1 CREATE (:PWNED) //` |
| `str`/`bytes` | `quote_string` escapes via `v.replace(...)`; overriding `replace` disabled escaping, overriding `__contains__` disabled the NUL guard |
| `_validate_procedure_name` | validated the value, then interpolated the *object* — f-strings call `__format__` |
| `_validate_yield` | validated `name.strip()` but emitted the original list |

Every one created a real `PWNED` node against FalkorDB 8.6.3. The fix is uniform: normalize to the exact base type (`str.__str__`, `bytes.decode`, `int()`, `float()`, `Decimal()`) *before* inspecting, and emit the value that was checked.

title: [PR] fix(asyncio): prevent connection pool kwargs mutation and await schema refresh
description:
### Description of change

1. **Fix `connection_pool.connection_kwargs` Mutation**: Calls `.copy()` on `conn.connection_pool.connection_kwargs` in `Cluster_Conn` before popping parameters. 2. **Await Schema Refresh**: Adds missing `await` to `self.schema.refresh(e.version)` in `AsyncGraph._query()` error handling.
3. **Unit Tests**: Adds `test_cluster_conn_preserves_connection_kwargs` to prevent regressions.

comments.text: Hi @Naseem77, I fixed the test case issue which was failing in CI. Please try to check again and let me know if any issues.

comments.author: naseem77
comments.text:
@SantoshDhaladhuli Thanks for this. I validated both fixes against a real 3-node cluster, not just by reading the diff. Both bugs are real and both fixes work.

**`Cluster_Conn` mutating the pool**

Popping straight off `connection_pool.connection_kwargs` strips `host`, `port`, `username`, `password` from the live pool:

```
main: #1 OK   #2 KeyError: 'host'
pr:   #1 OK   #2 OK   #3 OK
```

It only triggers when the same pool reaches `Cluster_Conn` twice, and `FalkorDB()` builds a fresh pool each time, so the normal path doesn't hit it. Narrower than it looks, but `.copy()` is clearly right.

**Missing `await`**

The important one. `GraphSchema.refresh` is `async def` and was called bare, so the refresh never ran. Same mismatch on both branches:

| | `schema.version` after |
|---|---|
| `main` | `0`, never refreshed |
| this PR | `999`, correct |

Your regression test also fails on unfixed `main`, which is exactly right.

**Non-blocking nit:**

```python
await self.schema.refresh(e.version)
raise e
```

If `refresh()` throws it replaces the `SchemaVersionMismatchException` the caller expects. Couldn't happen before since it never ran. `try/finally` would keep the original.

**On the Codecov failure:** it's flagging `falkordb/asyncio/graph.py` lines 91-92, which is the `await self.schema.refresh(...)` fix itself. Nothing in the suite raises a `SchemaVersionMismatchException`, so that handler never executes in CI. Your test covers the `.copy()` fix well (both cluster files hit 100%), but the `await` has no guard, meaning someone could drop it again and CI would stay green. A small unit test that mocks `execute_command` to raise `SchemaVersionMismatchException(7)` and asserts `refresh` was awaited would cover both lines and lock in the fix.

title: [PR] ci: use the shared report-scheduled-failure workflow
description:
## Summary
The `report-scheduled-failure` job that alerts the drivers team when the nightly run against `falkordb/falkordb:edge` breaks is duplicated across every official [FalkorDB client](https://docs.falkordb.com/getting-started/clients.html) — 8 copies in 7 repos (falkordb-ts, falkordb-py, falkordb-go, falkordb-rs ×2, falkordb-php, JFalkorDB, NFalkorDB). 7 of them are byte-identical.

[FalkorDB/.github#5](https://github.com/FalkorDB/.github/pull/5) hosts the job once as a reusable (`workflow_call`) workflow. This PR switches this repo over to it, replacing ~43 lines of duplicated shell per workflow with 6.

## Changes
- Replace the inlined `report-scheduled-failure` job body with a pinned `uses:` of the shared workflow, passing only `DRIVERS_GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL`.
- Keep `needs:`, `if:` and `permissions:` local — only this repo knows which jobs must have failed, and a called workflow can only downgrade the caller's token, never upgrade it, so `issues: write` has to be granted by the caller.

No behaviour change. The `github` context inside a called workflow belongs to the *caller*, so `github.repository`, `github.workflow` and the run URL in the alert resolve exactly as before, and the webhook secret is passed through explicitly.

## Testing
- `actionlint` passes on the modified workflow(s).
- Diffed the shared job body against the copy removed here: identical apart from the tracking issue title becoming an input.
- CI on this PR exercises the `uses:` reference resolving; the job itself only runs on a scheduled failure, so it will first fire on the next nightly `edge` run. Already verified end to end in [falkordb-ts#612](https://github.com/FalkorDB/falkordb-ts/pull/612).

## Memory / Performance Impact
N/A — CI configuration only.

## Related Issues
Depends on FalkorDB/.github#5 (merged).

title: [PR] build: bound dependencies to tested versions, release 1.7.0
description:
## What

Two commits:

1. **`build:`** — bound `redis` and `python-dateutil` to the versions this client is tested against
2. **`chore(release):`** — bump to `1.7.0`

```diff
 dependencies = [
-    "redis>=7.1.0",
-    "python-dateutil>=2.9.0",
+    "redis>=7.2,<8.2",
+    "python-dateutil>=2.9.0,<3",
 ]
```

## Why

Both dependencies had a lower bound only, so a fresh `pip install falkordb` always resolved to whatever was newest on PyPI. Nothing in this repo decided that — PyPI did.

That is exactly how redis 8.1 reached users: it added five pool-only keyword arguments to `ConnectionPool.connection_kwargs`, `Is_Cluster()` forwarded them to the synchronous `redis.Redis()` constructor, and every async client died with `TypeError: Redis.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'himport_registry'` before a single query ran. Fixed in #262, but it reached users first because nothing constrained the resolve.

Our `uv.lock` pins redis 7.4.0, which is why CI stayed green throughout — the lockfile governs this repo's own CI and nothing downstream. Consumers only ever see the range in `pyproject.toml`.

### The lower bound was also wrong

`falkordb/falkordb.py:4` does `from redis.driver_info import DriverInfo`. That module first appears in redis **7.2**, so `>=7.1.0` advertised a floor that fails on import. Raised to `>=7.2`.

### Why 1.7.0 and not 1.6.3

The bug fixes alone would be a patch, but narrowing the redis range changes which environments can install the client, which is more than a patch should do.

Since 1.6.2:
- **fix:** `Is_Cluster()` no longer forwards pool-only kwargs to `redis.Redis` (#262)
- **fix:** the execution plan parser attaches every sibling operation to its parent rather than nesting siblings under each other (#267)
- **build:** dependency bounds (this PR)

## Tradeoff worth naming

Upper bounds on a library are not free. If a user installs `falkordb` alongside a package that requires `redis>=8.2`, pip cannot satisfy both and the install fails with `ResolutionImpossible` — and there is nothing the user can do except wait for a release from us. That is the cost we are accepting in exchange for never shipping an untested transitive version again.

Two things keep that cost small:

- `<8.2` still allows redis 8.1.x, which is current, so no one is held back today
- #271 already runs the suite against the newest redis daily, so we learn about a new release from CI rather than from an issue

The bound should be raised as a routine chore whenever that daily job passes on a newer version — not left to drift until it blocks someone.

## Testing

- `103 passed` against `falkordb/falkordb:edge`
- fresh `pip install .` resolves redis **8.1.0** — inside the new bound, and working with #262
- `uv sync --extra test` leaves `uv.lock` unmodified

`uv.lock` carries only the three lines that had to change (the `falkordb` version and the two specifier strings). Note it was generated by a newer `uv` than 0.7.19 — running `uv lock` on an older uv

title: [PR] test: assert the client parses execution plans, and fix a plan parser bug
description:
Our CI runs against `falkordb/falkordb:edge`, which now resolves to the Rust engine, and the test suite failed 16 tests there before reaching any client code.

The tests asserted the *exact* operation tree that `GRAPH.EXPLAIN` / `GRAPH.PROFILE` returned — root op `Results`, then `Project`, then `Unwind`, and so on. That makes a planner change break the client's tests even when the client is fine, which is what happened: `Results` is gone, `Join` became `Union`, `MERGE` is rooted at `Commit` with a new `Include Pending` op, and a traverse renders as `(t)<-(r:Rider)`.

Which operations a query compiles into is the engine's business. What the client owes us is that it issues the command and parses the reply. So that's what these tests assert now, and they pass unchanged on **both** engines.

| | `falkordb:edge` (Rust) | `falkordb:v4.20.1` (C) |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 16 failed, 84 passed | passes |
| this branch | **100 passed** | **100 passed** |

## What the tests check now

`tests/plan_helpers.py` asserts, for any plan from any engine:

- every non-blank line of the raw reply became exactly one operation
- each operation sits as deep in the tree as its line was indented
- the name and the `| args` half were split apart correctly
- for profiles, statistics parsed, and `records_produced` matches the row count the *query* implies

The indentation comparison is the important one — it checks the parsed tree against the **raw reply**, so it fails if nesting is reconstructed wrongly.

## It caught a real parser bug

Writing that assertion turned up a genuine client bug, reproducible on both engines. When three or more operations share a nesting level, the parser attached the third to the second:

```
reply:                          parsed as:
Project                         Project
    Cartesian Product               Cartesian Product
        All Node Scan | (a)             All Node Scan | (a)
        All Node Scan | (b)             All Node Scan | (b)
        All Node Scan | (c)                 All Node Scan | (c)   <- wrong parent
```

`MATCH (a), (b), (c) RETURN *` is enough to hit it. The cause: each new sibling was pushed onto the stack in place of its parent, so the next sibling popped a sibling instead. Fixed in the first commit by keeping the parent on the stack.

This is why the old assertions couldn't catch it — they only ever used two-way branches, and comparing a plan to a hardcoded tree never checks the reply itself.

## Commits

1. **fix: attach every sibling operation to its parent when parsing a plan** — the bug above.
2. **test: assert the client parses execution plans, not which plan the engine picked** — the rework.
3. **test: use a slower query so the slowlog actually records it** — `UNWIND range(0, 200000)` runs in ~6ms on the Rust engine, below the ~10ms slowlog threshold, so nothing was recorded and the assertion indexed an empty list. Bumped to 1M rows (~25ms).

## Verification

Full suite against live servers on both engines,

title: [Issue] Async client broken with redis 8.1.0 (Is_Cluster forwards unknown connection_kwargs)
description:
A clean `pip install falkordb` today pulls redis 8.1.0, and the async client can't run anything:

```python
from falkordb.asyncio import FalkorDB

g = FalkorDB(host="localhost", port=6379).select_graph("t")
await g.query("RETURN 1")
# TypeError: Redis.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'himport_registry'
```

The sync client is fine, and redis 8.0.1 is fine — it's only async + redis >= 8.1.0.

## What's happening

`Is_Cluster()` in `falkordb/asyncio/cluster.py` forwards the whole `connection_kwargs` dict into a sync client:

```python
kwargs = pool.connection_kwargs.copy()
info = sync_redis.Redis(**kwargs).info(section="server")
```

redis 8.1.0's `ConnectionPool.__init__` now injects its own `himport_registry` into `connection_kwargs`, and `Redis.__init__` doesn't accept it. Since this probe runs during connection setup, every query fails before anything is sent.

## This is #235 again

#235 was the same thing with a different key — `path` instead of `himport_registry`, same function, same line, same `unexpected keyword argument`. It was fixed by special-casing that one key:

```python
if pool.connection_class is redis.UnixDomainSocketConnection:
    kwargs["unix_socket_path"] = kwargs.pop("path")
```

redis shipped 8.1.0 eleven days later and it broke again. Any future internal addition on redis's side will do the same.

## Suggested fix

Pass only what `Redis.__init__` actually accepts:

```python
_accepted = inspect.signature(sync_redis.Redis.__init__).parameters
kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k in _accepted}

info = sync_redis.Redis(**kwargs).info(section="server")
```

I patched this locally on falkordb 1.6.2 + redis 8.1.0 and async works again (`RETURN 1` → `[[1]]`). Filtering by signature also covers the `path` case, so the existing special-case could go.

The sync client already does something similar in `cluster.py` — it pulls fields out by name rather than forwarding everything, which is why it never broke.

## Also worth noting

- `redis>=7.1.0` has no upper bound, so this reaches users the moment redis publishes. Might be worth a cap until the fix ships.
- #258 (Bump redis 7.4.0 → 8.1.0) has been failing on Python 3.10–3.14 since 2026-07-30 with this exact `TypeError`. The fix above should make it green.

## Versions

falkordb 1.6.2, redis 8.1.0 (8.0.1 works), Python 3.11 / 3.12, macOS + Linux CI

comments.author: c-bjorn
comments.text:
Confirming this from an independent angle: we hit the identical `TypeError: Redis.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'himport_registry'` via `graphiti-core`'s `FalkorDriver` (not the async client directly — same `Is_Cluster` call path, same root cause you've already diagnosed here).

Our bisection against a disposable FalkorDB container: **redis-py 8.0.0 constructs cleanly; 8.1.0 fails 100% of the time.** Consistent with your 8.0.1-works finding — the break is squarely at the 8.0.x → 8.1.0 boundary.

Two things worth adding to what's already here:

1. Since this is the second time an internal redis-py addition (`path` in #235, now `himport_registry`) has broken this exact probe, filtering `connection_kwargs` by `inspect.signature(sync_redis.Redis.__init__)` (as you've already suggested) is the fix that stops this recurring — the `path` special-case from #235 is a symptom of the same underlying fragility.
2. Recommend adding an upper bound on `redis` in `falkordb-py`'s own package metadata (`redis>=7.1.0` currently has no ceiling). That absence is why this reaches every user on a fresh install by default, independent of when the real fix ships — a temporary ceiling decouples "users are broken" from "the fix has landed."

We've filed the user-facing half of this on the `graphiti-core` side (unpinned `redis` in that project's `falkordb` extra): [getzep/graphiti#1756](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/issues/1756). Cross-linking since a fix here resolves the underlying cause for both.

title: [PR] ci(test): run tests against latest, edge daily
description:
## Summary
CI validated every PR against `falkordb/falkordb:edge`, an unreleased build — so PRs could break for reasons unrelated to the change, and nothing verified the client against the FalkorDB version users actually run. This flips the default to the released `latest` image and moves `edge` to a daily scheduled run, which is where early warnings about upcoming FalkorDB releases belong.

## Changes
- Tests run against `falkordb/falkordb:latest` on pull requests, pushes to `main` and version tags (`v*.*.*` — newly added trigger, so releases are tested).
- New daily schedule (02:00 UTC) runs the same suite against `falkordb/falkordb:edge`.
- New `workflow_dispatch` with an optional `falkordb_image_tag` input to test an arbitrary tag on demand.
- The FalkorDB service container's image tag now comes from the shared resolver job instead of being hardcoded.
- `AGENTS.md` updated to match (local dev instructions + CI description).

Job names are unchanged, so existing branch-protection required checks keep working.

## The standard, in all seven clients
Every official client picks the image tag with the same expression:

```
${{ github.event.inputs.falkordb_image_tag || (github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'edge' || 'latest') }}
```

`latest` for pull requests, pushes, tags and releases; `edge` for the daily scheduled run; any tag on manual dispatch.

Clients that start FalkorDB with docker compose (falkordb-ts, falkordb-php) keep it in a workflow-level `FALKORDB_VERSION`, which compose reads as `falkordb/falkordb:${FALKORDB_VERSION:-latest}`.

Clients that run FalkorDB as a **service container** keep doing exactly that — the service container is the idiomatic mechanism and gets networking, health checks and cleanup from the runner for free. The tag still has a single definition, but it cannot be an `env:` variable: GitHub does not allow the `env` context in `jobs.<id>.services.<id>.image` ([context availability](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#context-availability)). A small `falkordb-version` job resolves it once and every job consumes it:

```yaml
jobs:
  falkordb-version:
    name: Resolve FalkorDB version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: resolve
        env:
          FALKORDB_VERSION: ${{ github.event.inputs.falkordb_image_tag || (github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'edge' || 'latest') }}
        run: echo "version=$FALKORDB_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  test:
    needs: falkordb-version
    services:
      falkordb:
        image: falkordb/falkordb:${{ needs.falkordb-version.outputs.version }}
```

## Failure notifications
The daily `edge` run posts to Google Chat when it fails. GitHub itself only emails whoever last edited the cron line, so without this the early-warning run would fail silently.

Add a Google Chat **incoming webhook** for the target space and store it as an Actions secret named `GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_UR

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
On why the image tag isn't simply set from `falkordb_image_tag`:

1. **`schedule` events cannot carry inputs.** Only `workflow_dispatch` can pass `inputs`, so the daily `edge` switch has to be derived from `github.event_name` — an input alone would never fire on the cron run.
2. **It can't be hoisted into `env:`.** GitHub does not allow the `env` context in `jobs.<id>.services.<id>.image`; the only contexts permitted there are `github, needs, strategy, matrix, vars, inputs` ([context availability](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#context-availability)). That is why the compose-based clients (falkordb-ts / falkordb-php) can use a plain `FALKORDB_VERSION` env var — compose runs inside a step, where `env` is available — while the service-container clients (py/go/rs/.NET) have to inline the expression.

So `falkordb_image_tag` is only a manual override; the `latest` vs `edge` decision has to live next to it. If you'd prefer a single named knob, the two alternatives are a small `setup` job whose output is consumed via `needs.<job>.outputs.tag`, or a repo-level `vars.FALKORDB_IMAGE_TAG` — happy to switch to either across all seven client PRs.

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
Good catch — reverted, FalkorDB runs as a service container again in all four clients that used one (falkordb-py, falkordb-go, falkordb-rs, NFalkorDB). The `docker run` step was a workaround for a constraint, not an improvement, and it gave up the runner's container networking, health checks and cleanup.

The single-knob standard is kept. Since GitHub does not allow the `env` context in `jobs.<id>.services.<id>.image` ([context availability](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#context-availability)), the tag is resolved once in a tiny job and consumed through `needs`, which *is* allowed there:

```yaml
jobs:
  falkordb-version:
    name: Resolve FalkorDB version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: resolve
        env:
          FALKORDB_VERSION: ${{ github.event.inputs.falkordb_image_tag || (github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'edge' || 'latest') }}
        run: echo "version=$FALKORDB_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  test:
    needs: falkordb-version
    services:
      falkordb:
        image: falkordb/falkordb:${{ needs.falkordb-version.outputs.version }}
```

Cost is one extra ~3s job per workflow. falkordb-ts and falkordb-php are unchanged — compose reads the env var directly, so they keep the plain workflow-level `FALKORDB_VERSION`.

Verified: this PR's runs pull `falkordb/falkordb:latest`, and a manual dispatch of the falkordb-rs coverage workflow with `falkordb_image_tag=edge` pulled `falkordb/falkordb:edge` into the service container ([run](https://github.com/FalkorDB/falkordb-rs/actions/runs/31615175267)), so the input, the schedule default and the health check all flow through correctly.

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
Review triage — thanks, three of these were real:

**Fixed**
- **Dispatch input default** (Copilot, falkordb-py): the input described itself as "defaults to latest" but had `default: ""`, showing a blank box. It now defaults to `latest` in every client. Scheduled runs are unaffected — `schedule` events carry no inputs, so they still resolve to `edge`.
- **Tag triggers** (CodeRabbit, falkordb-ts): falkordb-ts and falkordb-php publish bare semver tags (`6.7.0`), which `v*` never matched, so tagged releases were skipping CI entirely. Both now accept `v*` and `[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+`. falkordb-rs `coverage.yml` had no tag trigger at all and now has one.
- **JFalkorDB dispatch override** (Copilot): `maven.yml` hard-coded `FALKORDB_VERSION: latest` while the PR promised a manual override. It now defines the `falkordb_image_tag` input and reads it.

**Not applicable any more**
- `--pull=always` / shell-quoting of the image tag (Copilot, falkordb-rs + NFalkorDB): these targeted the interim `docker run` step, which has been reverted. FalkorDB is a service container again, and the runner runs `docker pull` for the service image on every run — confirmed in the logs of the `edge` dispatch. Nothing interpolates the tag into a shell command; the resolver passes it through `env:` and `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
- "`steps:` items are not indented" (Copilot, falkordb-go): false positive — a block sequence may sit at the same indentation as its key. The workflows parse and the jobs run.

**Declined**
- `persist-credentials: false` on `actions/checkout` (CodeRabbit, falkordb-go): valid hardening but unrelated to this change; it belongs in its own PR rather than widening a CI-image PR.
- "Add an agent section to `AGENTS.md`" (CodeRabbit, falkordb-py): misread — this repo's `AGENTS.md` is the conventional agent *instructions* file, not a catalogue of agents. The lines this PR touches only correct the FalkorDB image tag used locally and in CI.

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
**Who gets told when the daily `edge` run fails?** Until this commit: effectively nobody. GitHub emails only the user who *last modified the cron line* when a scheduled workflow fails, and only if they have Actions notifications enabled — so the early-warning job would have failed silently in the background.

Each scheduled workflow now ends with a `report-scheduled-failure` job:

```yaml
  report-scheduled-failure:
    needs: [falkordb-version, test]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'schedule' && contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
```

It opens an issue titled **"CI is failing against `falkordb/falkordb:edge`"** with a link to the run, or comments on that issue if it is already open — so a week of failures is one thread, not seven. Repository watchers get it through the normal issue notification path, which is the only channel maintainers actually read.

It only fires on `schedule`: manual dispatches and PR runs are already visible to whoever triggered them. `${{ }}` is never interpolated into the shell — the tag and run URL are passed through `env:`.

If you would rather have Slack, swap the single step for a webhook post; the job scaffolding stays the same.

comments.author: gkorland
comments.text:
Switched to Google Chat, as requested — the tracking issue is now only a fallback.

```yaml
  report-scheduled-failure:
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'schedule' && contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') }}
    env:
      GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL }}
    steps:
      - name: Notify Google Chat
        if: ${{ env.GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL != '' }}
        run: |
          jq -n --arg text "$text" '{text: $text}' > payload.json
          curl -sS --fail-with-body -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            -d @payload.json "$GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL"
```

**One thing is needed from you:** create an incoming webhook on the Google Chat space and store the URL as `GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL`. Setting it once at organisation level covers all seven clients:

```bash
gh secret set GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL --org FalkorDB --visibility all
```

Until it exists, the job falls back to opening/commenting on a tracking issue, so nothing is lost in the meantime. I did not set the secret myself — a webhook URL is a credential and shouldn't pass through here.

The rendered message:

> **FalkorDB/falkordb-py** — the daily `Test` run against `falkordb/falkordb:edge` failed.
> View the run
>
> `edge` is an unreleased FalkorDB build, so released users are unaffected: this is an early warning that the next FalkorDB release breaks this client.

I executed the generated step verbatim against a local HTTP listener to confirm the JSON body, the `jq` quoting and the `curl` invocation are correct. The text is assembled by `jq`, never string-interpolated, and no `${{ }}` reaches the shell; GitHub masks the webhook URL in logs.

title: [PR] Add latest-deps CI coverage and fix redis-py 8 async cluster probe compatibility
description:
`pip install falkordb` resolves against `pyproject.toml` constraints (not `uv.lock`), so users can get newer redis versions than lockfile CI exercises. This PR adds explicit latest-resolution CI coverage and addresses a real redis-py 8.x incompatibility discovered in the async cluster-detection path.

- **CI: add informational latest-dependencies test lane**
  - Added `test-latest-deps` job to `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
  - Installs with `uv sync --extra test --upgrade`, prints resolved versions, and runs tests.
  - Kept existing lockfile-based Python matrix job unchanged.
  - Marked `continue-on-error: true` so it acts as early warning without blocking.

- **Runtime compatibility: redis-py 8.x async/sync probe boundary**
  - Fixed async cluster probe in `falkordb/asyncio/cluster.py` to drop async-only `himport_registry` before constructing sync `redis.Redis(...)`.
  - Added regression coverage in `tests/test_async_db.py` to ensure async-only kwargs are not forwarded to the sync probe.

- **Dependency maintenance automation**
  - Extended existing `.github/dependabot.yml` policy alignment by setting `uv` updates to weekly (Actions already weekly), keeping lockfile and workflow pins from drifting.

- **Contributor policy documentation**
  - Added `CONTRIBUTING.md` section clarifying:

title: [PR] fix: only forward accepted kwargs from Is_Cluster to redis.Redis
description:
Fixes #261.

## Problem

The async client can't run a single query against redis >= 8.1.0:

```
TypeError: Redis.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'himport_registry'
```

What happens:

```
You call FalkorDB(...)
   ↓
Setup needs to know: is this a cluster or one server?
   ↓
calls Is_Cluster()
   ↓
to ask the server it needs a client, so it builds a temporary sync Redis
from the pool's connection_kwargs
   ↓
that dict is the argument set for Connection, and 8.1.0 added six fields to it:
himport_registry, maint_notifications_pool_handler, maint_notifications_config,
orig_host_address, orig_socket_timeout, orig_socket_connect_timeout
   ↓
Redis.__init__ accepts none of them → TypeError on himport_registry, the first one it hits
   ↓
FalkorDB(...) raises. No client is ever returned.
```

`connection_kwargs` is the argument set for `Connection`, not for `Redis` — redis-py builds connections with it directly:

```python
connection = self.connection_class(**self.connection_kwargs)
```

So the entries are legitimate connection parameters, they're just addressed to a different constructor. The two signatures overlap on the common fields (`host`, `port`, `db`, `ssl`, ...), which is why forwarding the dict worked for as long as it did. 8.1.0 added six parameters that `AbstractConnection` accepts and `Redis` does not, and the overlap stopped holding. `himport_registry` is simply the first one hit — each of the other five fails the same way.

Because the probe runs during connection setup, this raises before any command is sent — so it kills **every async query**, not just cluster deployments.

| client | redis 8.0.1 | redis 8.1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `falkordb.FalkorDB` | works | works |
| `falkordb.asyncio.FalkorDB` | works | unusable |

The sync client is unaffected: `falkordb/cluster.py` picks fields out by name instead of forwarding the whole dict.

Since `redis` is declared as `>=7.1.0` with no upper bound, a plain `pip install falkordb` resolves 8.1.0 and the async client is broken out of the box.

## Fix

Filter the kwargs against the `Redis.__init__` signature before forwarding.

I went with a signature filter rather than dropping `himport_registry` by name, because:

- 8.1.0 adds six such keys, not one — name-blocking is whack-a-mole
- this is a repeat of issue #235, which was the same crash in the same call with `path`. That was fixed by special-casing that one key, and redis shipped new `Connection` parameters 11 days later. A signature filter covers both and anything added later.

The `path` -> `unix_socket_path` translation is kept and still runs **before** the filter. It has to: `path` is not an accepted `Redis` parameter name, so if the filter ran first it would drop the key outright and the probe would silently connect over TCP to the default host instead of the unix socket. A quiet misconnect is worse than the `TypeError` this PR removes, so the rename can't be folded into the filter.

title: [PR] Align EXPLAIN/PROFILE test assertions to the new edge execution plan format
description:
The `falkordb:edge` server changed its execution plan printout, breaking test assertions that compare plan trees exactly (`assert 'Project' == 'Results'`, `assert 'Commit' == 'Merge'`).

Verified against `falkordb/falkordb:edge`, the plan format now differs as follows:

| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| `Results` root operation | removed — plans start at `Project` / `Distinct` |
| `Join` (for `UNION`) | `Union` |
| `Conditional Traverse \| (t)->(r:Rider)` | `Conditional Traverse \| (t)<-(r:Rider)` |

title: [Issue] `FalkorDB.from_url("unix://…")` raises `TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'path'`
description:
## Summary

The async client cannot connect over a Unix domain socket. Any `FalkorDB.from_url("unix:///path/to/socket.sock?db=N")` raises a `TypeError` **before any I/O**, during the synchronous cluster-detection probe in `falkordb.asyncio.cluster.Is_Cluster`.

`Is_Cluster` copies the **async** connection pool's `connection_kwargs` and passes them verbatim to a **synchronous** `redis.Redis(**kwargs)`. For a Unix-socket connection, redis-py stores the socket path under the key `path`, but the synchronous `redis.Redis.__init__` only accepts `unix_socket_path`, so construction fails with `unexpected keyword argument 'path'`.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| `falkordb` | **1.6.1** (latest release; `master` has the identical code) |
| `redis` (redis-py) | 7.4.1 |
| Python | 3.12 |
| OS | macOS (arm64); not OS-specific — any Unix-socket connection hits it |

## Steps to reproduce

No running server is required. The failure happens at client construction, before any connection is opened.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduces FalkorDB.from_url("unix://...") TypeError. No server needed."""

import importlib.metadata as md
import traceback

import redis
import redis.asyncio as aredis
from falkordb.asyncio import FalkorDB

print("falkordb:", md.version("falkordb"))
print("redis:   ", md.version("redis"))

UNIX_URL = "unix:///tmp/falkordb.sock?db=0"  # path need not exist for this repro

# 1) What does redis-py's async pool store for a unix:// URL?
pool = aredis.from_url(UNIX_URL, decode_responses=True).connection_pool
kwargs = dict(pool.connection_kwargs)
print("\n[1] async unix pool")
print("    connection_class :", pool.connection_class.__name__)
print("    connection_kwargs:", sorted(kwargs))
print("    socket path stored under key:", "'path'" if "path" in kwargs else "(absent)")

# 2) The root cause: the SYNC constructor rejects 'path' (it wants
#    'unix_socket_path'). Is_Cluster passes these async kwargs straight through.
print("\n[2] sync redis.Redis(**async_unix_kwargs)  (what Is_Cluster does)")
kwargs["ssl"] = pool.connection_class is aredis.SSLConnection
try:
    redis.Redis(**kwargs)
    print("    -> constructed OK (unexpected)")
except TypeError as exc:
    print(f"    -> TypeError: {exc}")

# 3) The user-visible failure via the public API.
print('\n[3] FalkorDB.from_url("unix://...")')
try:
    FalkorDB.from_url(UNIX_URL)
    print("    -> constructed OK (unexpected)")
except TypeError as exc:
    print(f"    -> TypeError: {exc}")
    print("\n--- traceback (note the frame inside Is_Cluster) ---")
    traceback.print_exc()
```

## Actual output

```text
falkordb: 1.6.1
redis:    7.4.1

[1] async unix pool
    connection_class : UnixDomainSocketConnection
    connection_kwargs: ['db', 'decode_responses', 'path']
    socket path stored under key: 'path'

[2] sync redis.Redis(**async_unix_kwargs)  (what Is_Cluster does)
    -> TypeError: Redis.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'path'

[3] FalkorDB.from_url("unix://...")

title: [PR] Fix async unix-socket connection crashing in Is_Cluster (#235)
description:
Fixes #235.

## Problem

`FalkorDB.from_url("unix:///path/to/socket.sock")` on the async client raises a
`TypeError` before any I/O, during the synchronous cluster-detection probe in
`falkordb.asyncio.cluster.Is_Cluster`.

`Is_Cluster` copies the async pool's `connection_kwargs` and passes them to a
synchronous `redis.Redis(**kwargs)`. For a Unix-socket connection, redis-py
stores the socket path under the key `path`, but the synchronous
`redis.Redis.__init__` only accepts `unix_socket_path`, so construction fails
with `unexpected keyword argument 'path'`. Any async unix-socket connection is
affected.

## Fix

When the pool uses a `UnixDomainSocketConnection`, translate the `path` kwarg to
`unix_socket_path` before building the synchronous probe. Other connection types
are untouched. After the fix the sync client is constructed normally and the
only remaining failure for an unreachable socket is the expected connection
error, not a `TypeError`.

## Test

Adds `test_is_cluster_unix_socket_does_not_crash_on_path_kwarg` in
`tests/test_async_db.py`. It is server-free: it points at a non-existent socket
and asserts `Is_Cluster` now fails (if at all) with a connection error rather
than a `TypeError`. Without the fix the test fails with the original
`TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'path'`; with it, it passes.

`uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run ruff check .`, and `uv run mypy
falkordb/` all pass.

This change was prepared by an AI agent under my direction; I reviewed and
verified it (reproduced the crash, confirmed the fix, and checked the red/green
behavior of the regression test).

title: [Issue] select_graph(''): misleading TypeError "Expected a string parameter, but received <class 'str'>" for empty string
description:
### Summary

`select_graph()` validates its argument with:

```python
if not isinstance(graph_id, str) or graph_id == "":
    raise TypeError(f"Expected a string parameter, but received {type(graph_id)}.")
```

(present in both `falkordb/falkordb.py` and `falkordb/asyncio/falkordb.py`; unchanged since 2023.)

When the caller passes an **empty string**, the second clause trips and the message prints:

```
TypeError: Expected a string parameter, but received <class 'str'>.
```

i.e. "expected a string, received a string" — the value *is* a `str`, just empty. In a production incident (via graphiti-core, see getzep/graphiti#1650) this message sent us debugging a non-existent type-corruption problem for a while.

### Suggested fix

Split the two conditions so each failure mode gets an accurate message, e.g.:

```python
if not isinstance(graph_id, str):
    raise TypeError(f"Expected a string parameter, but received {type(graph_id)}.")
if graph_id == "":
    raise ValueError("graph_id must be a non-empty string.")
```

Happy to submit this as a PR if wanted.

title: [Issue] GraphSchema cache returns wrong property names after graph delete/recreate
description:
## Summary

When a graph is deleted **externally** (raw `GRAPH.DELETE`, another process, crashed process whose `finally{}` didn't run) without going through the `Graph.delete()` method, `GraphSchema.properties` retains the old graph's property key mapping. If a new graph is created under the same name with a different property-key registration order, `RETURN n` (compact format) silently maps `attr_id`s to **wrong property names**, returning corrupt data.

`RETURN properties(n)` (MAP format) is unaffected because it inlines key strings and never touches the schema cache.

## Versions

- **falkordb-py**: 1.6.1
- **FalkorDB server**: graph module ver 41811
- **Python**: 3.12

## Reproduction

```python
from falkordb import FalkorDB

db = FalkorDB()
gname = "repro_schema_cache_bug"

# Cleanup
try:
    db.connection.execute_command("GRAPH.DELETE", gname)
except Exception:
    pass

# Phase 1: build graph A with property order [id, name, color, size]
g = db.select_graph(gname)
g.query("CREATE (n:Item) SET n.id='i1', n.name='Widget', n.color='red', n.size=10")

# Populate the schema cache
res = g.query("MATCH (n:Item) RETURN n")
assert res.result_set[0][0].properties == {
    "id": "i1", "name": "Widget", "color": "red", "size": 10
}
print(f"Graph A cache: {g.schema.properties}")
# → ['id', 'name', 'color', 'size']

# Phase 2: external delete — bypasses Graph.delete() / schema.clear()
db.connection.execute_command("GRAPH.DELETE", gname)
# Cache is now STALE

# Phase 3: recreate graph B — same property names, different registration order
g_new = db.select_graph(gname)
g_new.query("CREATE (n:Item) SET n.id='i2', n.size=20, n.color='blue', n.name='Gadget'")
# Graph B property keys: ['id', 'size', 'color', 'name']

# Phase 4: read with stale cache → WRONG data
res_compact = g.query("MATCH (n:Item) RETURN n")
compact = res_compact.result_set[0][0].properties

res_map = g.query("MATCH (n:Item) RETURN properties(n)")
correct = dict(res_map.result_set[0][0])

print(f"RETURN n:              {compact}")
print(f"RETURN properties(n):  {correct}")
# RETURN n:              {'id': 'i2', 'name': 20, 'color': 'blue', 'size': 'Gadget'}
# RETURN properties(n):  {'id': 'i2', 'size': 20, 'color': 'blue', 'name': 'Gadget'}
# 'name' got 20 (size's value), 'size' got 'Gadget' (name's value)
```

## Root cause

`GraphSchema.get_property(idx)` (`graph_schema.py:135-153`) only refreshes on `IndexError` — when `idx >= len(self.properties)`. It does **not** detect when:

1. The graph was deleted and recreated (cache too long — stale entries from old graph)
2. The property key order changed (same length but different mapping)

`Graph.delete()` calls `self.schema.clear()` before `GRAPH.DELETE`, which protects **same-object** delete/recreate. But any external deletion (another connection, raw command, killed process) leaves the cache stale.

The server **does** send a schema version mismatch in some cases, but this is only checked in `_query()` at the query level — `__parse_entity_pr

title: [PR] fix(params): wrap parameter and dict-map keys in backticks

## Summary
Fixes a Cypher syntax error when a parameter name — or a key inside a parameter dictionary — contains characters that are not valid in a bare Cypher identifier (e.g. `@type`, UUIDs with hyphens like `0be6ffd7-3844-46a3-a699-bf3b77c573cd`).

- `falkordb/helpers.py`: wrap each dictionary key in backticks when serializing a `dict` value to an inline Cypher map literal.
- `tests/test_graph.py` & `tests/test_async_graph.py`: regression tests covering `@type`, hyphenated UUID keys as parameter names, and as dict-property keys round-tripped through a parameter.

params_header += f"`{key}`" + "=" + stringify_param_value(value) + " "

title: [Issue] Silent process crash after GRAPH.CONFIG TIMEOUT fires on query
description:
## Summary

When FalkorDB's server-side query timeout fires (`GRAPH.CONFIG TIMEOUT`), the FalkorDB Python driver (v1.6.0) can crash the Python process silently — no Python traceback, no exception, no signal. The process simply exits.

The crash occurs on the **next FalkorDB operation** after the initial `ResponseError: Query timed out` — the connection enters an unhealthy state, and the subsequent operation crashes at the C-level redis client, bypassing Python's exception handling entirely.

## Environment

- FalkorDB Docker: `falkordb/falkordb:latest`
- FalkorDB Python driver: **1.6.0**
- Python: 3.12.8
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (WSL2)
- Connection: synchronous `FalkorDB()` client

## Repro

1. Start FalkorDB with a low query timeout:
   ```bash
   docker exec <container> redis-cli GRAPH.CONFIG SET TIMEOUT 1000
   ```

2. Populate the graph with 800+ entities (enough to make full-text search queries take >1s)

3. Run a query that exceeds the timeout:
   ```python
   from falkordb import FalkorDB
   fdb = FalkorDB(host="localhost", port=6380)
   fg = fdb.select_graph("my_graph")
   
   # First query — triggers ResponseError: Query timed out
   try:
       fg.query("CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO', $query) "
                "YIELD relationship AS rel, score "
                "MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m:Entity) "
                "RETURN e.name, e.fact, score LIMIT 20",
                params={"query": "tax obligations company law enforcement"})
   except Exception as e:
       print(f"Caught: {e}")  # ResponseError: Query timed out
   
   # Second query — process crashes silently here
   fg.query("RETURN 1")  # Never returns, process exits with no traceback
   ```

4. **Observed:** The process exits silently after the second query. No Python exception. No traceback. No signal.

5. **Expected:** A `redis.exceptions.ConnectionError` or `ResponseError` should be raised, allowing the calling code to reconnect or handle the error gracefully.

## Additional context

- The crash is reproducible when the connection is reused after a query timeout
- `asyncio.wait_for()` wrapping does not help because the crash occurs at the C extension level
- Our workaround: raise TIMEOUT to 10000+ and run all FalkorDB access in subprocess isolation so a driver crash cannot take down the main application process
- The issue may be related to the underlying `redis-py` async connection pool state management after a server-side timeout error

## Impact

Any long-running Python application (web server, background worker) that holds a persistent FalkorDB connection will crash if a query times out, with no opportunity to recover. The crash is silent and provides no diagnostic information.

title: [Issue] quote_string does not escape newlines, breaking CYPHER params header
description:
## Bug Description

`helpers.quote_string()` escapes backslashes and double quotes but does **not** escape newline characters (`\n`). When a string parameter containing newlines is serialized into the `CYPHER` params header by `_build_params_header()`, the header breaks across multiple lines, causing FalkorDB to parse it as an incomplete command.

## Reproduction

```python
from falkordb.helpers import quote_string

s = "line1\nline2"
result = quote_string(s)
print(repr(result))  # '"line1\nline2"' — contains literal newline
```

When this value is used in a parameterized query:

```python
from falkordb import FalkorDB

db = FalkorDB()
graph = db.select_graph("test")
graph.query("UNWIND $items AS item RETURN item", params={"items": [{"text": "hello\nworld"}]})
```

FalkorDB receives:
```
CYPHER items=[{text:"hello
world"}] UNWIND $items AS item RETURN item
```

The newline splits the command, and FalkorDB tries to parse `CYPHER items=[{text:"hello` as a complete command, producing:

```
ResponseError: errMsg: Invalid input at end of input: expected '='
line: 1, column: 13, offset: 12
errCtx: CYPHER items
errCtxOffset: 12
```

## Expected Behavior

`quote_string()` should escape newlines (and other control characters) so the params header remains a single line:

```python
def quote_string(v):
    if isinstance(v, bytes):
        v = v.decode()
    elif not isinstance(v, str):
        return v
    if len(v) == 0:
        return '""'

    v = v.replace("\\", "\\\\")
    v = v.replace('"', '\\"')
    v = v.replace("\n", "\\n")
    v = v.replace("\r", "\\r")
    v = v.replace("\t", "\\t")

    return f'"{v}"'
```

## Impact

Any application storing multi-line text (summaries, descriptions, narratives) in graph node/edge properties will hit this when using parameterized queries with the `CYPHER` params header format.

## Environment

- `falkordb` Python client: 1.6.0 (latest)
- FalkorDB server: latest Docker image
- Python: 3.13

title: [Issue] ci: Pin GitHub Actions dependencies to commit SHAs for supply-chain security
description:
## Summary

All third-party GitHub Actions in this repository's workflows are currently referenced by **mutable version tags** (e.g., `actions/checkout@v4`). This is a supply-chain security risk — tags can be force-pushed to point to malicious code.

## Recommendation

Pin all third-party GitHub Actions to their **full commit SHA** while preserving the version in a comment for readability:

```yaml
# Before (insecure)
uses: actions/checkout@v4

# After (secure)
uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4
```

## Affected Files

- `.github/workflows/lint.yml`
- `.github/workflows/pypi-publish.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/spellcheck.yml`
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`

## Actions Pinned

10 action references across 4 workflow file(s).

## References

- [GitHub Security Hardening Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)

title: [PR] feat(ingestion): agentic per-document strategy selection
description:
## Updates (alignment with GraphRAG-Server demo-v2 + review fixes)

demo-v2 has no planner, so nothing was ported from it. It was used as the reference for the option menu (chunkers, `exact` / `llm_verified` resolvers, GLiNER vs LLM extraction). The SDK already passes the ontology's relation types to the extractor and already skips the planner for structured sources (now covered by a test).

### Fixes
- **Clamping no longer discards valid plans:**
  - A `chunk_size` given alone (e.g. 100) gets an overlap that fits.
  - `Infinity` / `NaN` are dropped instead of raising `OverflowError`.
  - Quoted `key: 'value'` replies are parsed.
  - `PARAM_SPECS` defaults now match the constructors (`max_tokens` 384, `soft_threshold` 0.65).
- **GLiNER threshold is no longer tunable by the planner:** thresholds are model-specific and the planner can't know which model is loaded.
- **Each strategy is built on its own:** only the slots the caller left unset are built. If one can't be built, it falls back to its default and the rest of the plan still applies.
- **`structural` without document elements is reported as `sentence`:** in text mode it only ever delegated to the sentence chunker.
- **Stricter heuristic:** it now needs 2+ Markdown headings, or a heading plus 3+ list items. A single `- ` line no longer counts.
- **Better planner sample:** long documents are sampled from the start, middle and end, instead of only the first 1500 chars.

### New
- **Cost ceiling:** `LLMIngestionPlanner(chunkers=, extractors=, resolvers=, max_llm_pairs=)` limits what the planner may pick. The prompt only lists the allowed options. The `llm_verified` pair budget is capped at 500 by default (was 5000), so document text can't force the expensive strategies.
- **`IngestionResult.metadata["plan"]`** records the planner, the plan (strategies, params, reason), where each slot came from (`caller` / `planner` / `default`), and notes on any fallback.
- **Planner failures are logged at WARNING** (were DEBUG), and a fallback plan's reason says why.

### Tests
- New unit tests for each fix.
- Facade tests for metadata, batch + `auto`, caller slots, planner failure, and a table never running the planner.
- An end-to-end run against a live FalkorDB using a scripted LLM: file, text and batch ingest, an injected "expensive" plan, `finalize()`, retrieval and an agentic answer.

### Not in this PR
`auto` for `update()`; progress callbacks; structured diagnostics.

- **core models**: `AgentStep`, `AgentTrace`, `ScoredPath`, `SkillResult`.
- **storage**: `GraphStore.pagerank()` and `weighted_neighbors()`. `weighted_neighbors` now returns one row per neighbour in a fixed order and skips the internal `SAME_AS` / `DISTINCT_FROM` edges.

- `LLMResponse.tool_calls` is now parsed, and `finish_reason` is added. OpenAI-shaped dicts are still accepted.

- **Native tool calling** when the LLM supports it; otherwise the ReAct text loop is the fallback (`mode="auto" | "native" | "react"`).

- **Refusals instead of failures:** a bad call comes back to the model as `Refused: <tool> did not run: <why>` instead of ending the run. That covers an unknown tool, bad or invalid-JSON arguments, and a name that matches nothing.

title: [PR] fix(dedup): stop caching description vectors on entity nodes
description:
## Why

The LLM judge (#327) cached every description's vector **on its entity node** (`description_embedding` + `description_embedding_hash`). That is up to 1,024 floats per entity (20–63 KB serialised), carried by every read of the node. In the GraphRAG Server this caused:

- merge previews over the egress cap (413)
- undo records over their cap, so merges could not be undone
- entitlement projections that had to scrub the field
- the vector showing in Node Detail
- extra size in every graph, save point and export

## What

- **No cache at all.** Description vectors are computed each run and never written to the graph. There is no extra graph and no new module. `_desc_vectors` goes back to its pre-cache form.
- **Old graphs get cleaned.** Each judge run removes both properties from any entity that still has them. It works in batches of 1,000, and a failure only logs a warning; the next run finishes the job.
- **Never copied in the meantime.** Both keys stay in `_NEVER_CARRY` and `_NEVER_CARRY_ON_RECONCILE` (shared as `LEGACY_DESC_KEYS`). Merges and ingest reconciliation run before the judge's cleanup, or without it when `judge=False`, so an old duplicate's vector must never land on a clean survivor.
- **Docs.** The CHANGELOG, `docs/storage.mdx` and `docs/api-reference.mdx` now say the vectors are not stored.

Net change: about 215 lines removed. Dedup decisions are unchanged. The trade-off is that every `finalize()` re-embeds every description.

## Tests

- **Unit:** nothing writes a description vector to a node, the cleanup query runs, and a failed cleanup does not abort the judge phase.
- **Live FalkorDB (one-off):** a graph of 2,500 nodes carrying the old properties had 0 left after `finalize()`.
- **Full suite with `RUN_INTEGRATION=1`:** 2287 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_structured_guards.py::…::test_a_second_proposal_reducing_to_the_same_signature_is_refused`, also fails on `main` without this change.

## Rollout

The GraphRAG Server stays pinned at `2f808d5` until after the Verdantix demonstration (6 Oct 2026). No pin bump is requested here. After the bump, the server's workarounds can be removed: `entity_merge.py`, `merge_provenance.py`, `retrieval_controls.py`, `projection_scrub.py` and `NodeDetail.tsx`.

title: [PR] fix(judge): LLM type gate stops cross-type merges in finalize dedup
description:
## Summary

The finalize-time judge (`EntityJudgeDeduplicator`) groups candidate pairs by name/description similarity and asks the LLM to partition them. Cross-type pairs — a `Person` next to a `Date`, an `Organization` next to a `Location` — were reaching the model through shared descriptions, and the prompt told it that *"type labels are sometimes wrong, so the same entity can appear under two labels"*. On a 36-doc business corpus this produced **17 wrong merges** with a gpt-4o-mini judge, including people merged into dates and suppliers merged into customers.

This PR adds an LLM type gate ahead of grouping and removes the prompt allowance. The gate is strictly reductive (it can only drop candidates), fail-open, and uses no hardcoded label list, so it works with whatever ontology extraction produced.

## Changes

- **`storage/judge_dedup.py` — LLM type gate.** One batched call per finalize asks the judge model, for each distinct label pair among the nominated candidates, whether two entities of those types could ever be the same real-world referent. A `NO` removes every candidate pair carrying those labels before grouping. Verdicts are cached on the instance; unanswered pairs and failed calls fall through to the judge unchanged.
- **`storage/judge_dedup.py` — prompt.** Replaced the "labels may be wrong" sentence with an explicit rule that entities of different kinds are never the same referent.
- New judge stats: `type_gated`, `type_gate_calls`.
- **`tests/test_judge_dedup.py`.** `ScriptedLLM` answers gate prompts (per-pair overrides via `gate_verdicts`); new test asserts cross-type pairs never reach the model and a gate `NO` blocks a pair regardless of names.

## Test Plan

- [x] All existing tests pass (`pytest tests/ -q`) — 376 passed in the judge/dedup/resolution/finalize selection, no regressions
- [x] New tests added for new functionality — `test_cross_family_pairs_never_reach_the_model`
- [x] Lint passes (`ruff check src/`)

## Notes

Measured on live FalkorDB graphs:

| Corpus | Model | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Business, 36 docs (3 orgs × aliases, 15 employees, 12 customers, 2 traps) | gpt-4o-mini | 13 correct / **17 wrong** | 8 correct / **0 wrong** |
| Business, 36 docs | gpt-4.1 (3 runs) | – | 17–18 correct / **0 wrong** |
| Research institute, 40 docs (6 aliases, 3 look-alike traps) | gpt-4.1 | 0 wrong, 1348 candidates → 78 judge calls | 0 wrong, 532 candidates → **32 judge calls** |

All distractor traps held in every run. Judge LLM calls drop 60–70%.

No API change: `finalize(judge=True, judge_llm=...)` behaves as before; the gate uses the same model as the judge.

title: [PR] Record what the judge decided about each pair
description:
## The problem

The judge reports how a run went — how many candidates it saw, how often the two passes agreed, how many merged. All of those are properties of the run across the whole graph.

None of them answers the question a reader actually has when one proposed merge is put in front of them: **how sure are we about these two**. And a run figure shown next to a single pair reads as though it were about that pair. A caller building a review UI on `judge_stats` today has nothing else to reach for, so that misreading is the likely outcome rather than an unlikely one.

## What this adds

`FinalizeResult.judge_pair_decisions` — one entry per pair the judge actually considered:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `a`, `b`, `a_name`, `b_name` | the two entities |
| `similarity` | what the gates measured, before the model was asked anything |
| `votes` / `passes` | how many passes called them the same, out of how many saw them |
| `verdict` | `same`, `split`, `different`, `unjudged` |
| `merged` | whether they ended up merged |

Only pairs that reached the judge appear. A pair no gate brought forward was never a question.

## What it deliberately does not add

**No probability, no score, no confidence band.** The judge does not produce one, and deriving a number here would put a confidence on the record that nothing measured. The parts are reported instead, so a caller that wants bands can form them and will know what its own bands mean. Banding is a presentation decision and belongs to whoever is presenting.

## Details worth a second look

- `votes` and `merged` are separate, because agreement is not merger — a pair can be agreed and still be kept apart by the grouping rules.
- A pair in a set whose prompt failed is `unjudged`, not a disagreement. It was judged fewer times than the run was configured for, so "1 of 2 passes" would report a split that never happened.
- The list is cleared at the **start** of a run, not the end. Every early return otherwise leaves the previous run's decisions attributed to this one.
- Capped at 200 and ordered by similarity, so a graph with thousands of near-misses cannot turn one field into the whole payload, and the cut falls on the least similar.
- `same2 = {}` in the single-pass branch is new support for the per-pair record, not a fix to existing behaviour — it was previously bound and read only under `vote=True`.

## Tests

Eight new cases in `test_judge_dedup.py`:

- `test_pair_decisions_are_recorded_for_the_pair_that_merged`
- `test_a_pair_the_passes_split_on_is_not_reported_as_agreed`
- `test_a_single_pass_run_never_claims_two_votes`
- `test_a_rejected_pair_is_recorded_as_different`
- `test_decisions_are_ordered_by_similarity`
- `test_a_run_with_no_candidates_records_no_decisions`
- `test_decisions_do_not_survive_into_the_next_run`
- `test_protected_pairs_are_never_offered_as_decisions`

Full SDK unit suite: **2076 passed, 226 skipped, 0 failed.** Each of the two commits is green on its own.

title: [PR] Deduplication: LLM-judged cross-document dedup in finalize() — nominate, group, judge twice, merge or link
description:
## Deduplication — LLM-judged cross-document dedup in `finalize()`

Part of FalkorDB/research#88. Stacked on #326. This is where cross-document duplicates are merged; ingest stays exact-match only.

### What `finalize()` does now
1. remove NULL-name stubs → 2. **`deduplicate_entities(resolver=..., judge=True)`** (the judge embeds and stores the names it reads) → 3. **name embeddings on every entity still missing one** (after dedup, so a duplicate about to be removed is not embedded) → 4. relationship embeddings → 5. indexes

### 3a. Exact-name dedup across all documents
Same normalised name + same label → one node. `descriptions` = every member's list, `description` = the `" | "` join, absorbed names → `aliases`, edges moved to the survivor **before** the loser is deleted.

### 3b. The judge (`storage/judge_dedup.py`) — similarity nominates, the LLM decides twice
- **Nominate, no LLM:** top-10 name neighbours ≥ 0.65 · top-10 description neighbours ≥ 0.55 · "A's name appears in B's description"
- **Group:** dense sets of ≤ 8 — more than half of a set's pairs must be nominated, so a chain A–B–C–D (exactly half) cannot form; a straddling edge is its own 2-member set and agreements are unioned within one set only, so sets never chain into one merge. Packed into ≤ 3,000-token prompts; entity text is flattened, quoted and declared untrusted
- **Judge, pass 1:** "which of these are the same real-world thing? return groups" — names, labels, descriptions only
- **Judge, pass 2** (`judge_vote=True`, default)**:** same sets, shuffled and reversed; an answer that changes with the order is a guess. `judge_vote=False` = one pass, its groups merge, nothing is linked. A set whose prompt failed in either pass is left unjudged
- **Both agree → merge:** survivor by the finalize rank (table row > degree > longest description); `descriptions` list + `" | "` join; **every member's label** set on the survivor and recorded in `merged_labels`, so a later merge carries it on and the primary label never flips; other names in `aliases`; edges moved first, then the loser deleted
- **One agrees → link:** a `SAME_AS` edge (`source='llm_judge'`); both nodes stay
- **Neither → nothing**

`judge_llm` defaults to the GraphRAG LLM; a gpt-4.1-class model is recommended (9 wrong merges vs 51 for gpt-4o-mini on the benchmark). `judge_vote=False` halves cost at ~3× wrong merges. `finalize(judge=False)` skips the judge but the resolver pass still runs; **`finalize(resolve=False, judge=False)` is the LLM-free finalize**. The standalone `deduplicate_entities()` keeps making no LLM calls by default — the judge there is opt-in (`judge=True`). `FinalizeResult` gains `entities_linked`, `judge_llm_calls`, `judge_stats`.

### Also
The extraction prompt now asks for descriptions that separate similarly named entities (role, place, date) and never borrow another entity's facts — the judge decides on descriptions.

### Measured
Two-pass vote cut wrong merges by two thirds at 2× judge cost. Live 3-

title: [PR] Deduplication: LLMVerifiedResolution rework — unified candidates, batching, family gate, second vote (opt-in)
description:
## Deduplication — LLMVerifiedResolution rework (opt-in per-document resolver)

Part of FalkorDB/research#88. Stacked on #325. Not the default anywhere — pass `resolver=LLMVerifiedResolution(llm, embedder)` to `ingest()` to resolve per document with an LLM; cross-document dedup is `finalize()`'s job (PR 5 below).

### 1. Unified same/cross-label candidate stage, soft floor 0.65
**Problem:** candidates were bucketed by label, so two surface forms of one entity that shared a label were only compared by name, and the cross-label pass only looked at pairs whose labels differed — 28 % reach at any threshold.
**Fix:** one stage embeds `"name: description"` for every node and nominates pairs above 0.65 regardless of label (`cross_label_max_pairs=200`). Measured on 216 gold / 39 must-not-merge pairs, 3 runs: +22 true merges (+26 % recall), 0 extra wrong merges.

### 2. Batched verification, 5 pairs per call
**Fix:** `verification_token_budget=4000`, `verification_max_pairs_per_call=5`. Larger batches gave bimodal results on identical input. 5× fewer calls than one pair per call for 2.3 fewer merges and no wrong merge.

### 3. Label-family gate + cross-label second vote
**Problem:** the unified stage let Person|Institution, Person|Place pairs reach the LLM; 33 of 50 wrong merges on the benchmark were cross-family.
**Fix:** pairs whose labels are in different families are dropped before the LLM; a cross-label YES is re-asked with A/B swapped and merged only on agreement. Wrong merges 50 → 10 over three end-to-end runs, must-not-merge traps 1 → 0.

### 4. Same merge rules as everywhere else
Both merge loops write the `descriptions` list + `" | "` join via the shared helper, record every absorbed label in `merged_labels`, and re-point edges before the write. `max_llm_pairs` now logs how many pairs were sent / dropped; the unused `_VERIFY_PROMPT` is gone.

### Verification
Full suite: **1229 passed, 41 skipped**; ruff clean.
