title: [PR] Deduplication: every merge keeps all descriptions and labels; ingest resolves with exact match only
description:
## Deduplication — every merge keeps all descriptions and labels; ingest resolves with exact match only

Part of FalkorDB/research#88. Stacked on #324.

### 1. One exact-match merge function
**Problem:** the normalised-name merge existed once per strategy.
**Fix:** `exact_match_merge()` in `base.py`; `ExactMatchResolution` delegates to it and gains `llm` / `cross_label_merge` / `force_summary_threshold` knobs (all off in the default). `flatten_remap()` collapses merge chains (dup → A, A → B) before edges are re-pointed, so nothing is rewritten to an id that no longer exists.

### 2. Every merge, everywhere, follows three rules
- **Descriptions:** the survivor keeps every member's description — `descriptions` is a list (`["desc1", "desc2", …]`), `description` the same texts joined with `" | "` for the fulltext index, search and prompts. `set_merged_descriptions()` writes both and reads either form, so older survivors merge the same way.
- **Labels:** a survivor that absorbed a differently typed node records it in `merged_labels`; `GraphStore.upsert_nodes` promotes those to real Cypher labels, so `MATCH (n:Engineer)` finds a Person that absorbed an Engineer (before: 0 rows).
- **Edges:** relationship endpoints are re-pointed to the survivor before anything is written.

### 3. Ingest resolves with exact match only — zero LLM
**Fix:** `GraphRAG._default_resolver()` returns `ExactMatchResolution(llm=None, cross_label_merge=False)` for `ingest()` and `update()`: same name + same label within the document, no summaries, no cross-label merges. A resolver at ingest only ever sees one document, so the cross-document duplicates that matter are unreachable there; they are merged once, in `finalize()`.

### 4. Warn once when a graph was never finalized
**Fix:** `retrieve()` / `completion()` warn once per pending batch if documents were ingested and no dedup pass ran; `deduplicate_entities()` / `finalize()` clear it.

### Verification
Full suite: **1127 passed, 41 skipped**; ruff clean. `test_merge_invariants.py` pins the three rules for exact match.

title: [PR] feat(structured): tables declared on the ontology, one node for a row and its prose mention
description:
Closes FalkorDB/research#82 · design in #290 · supersedes #74

## What

GraphRAG-SDK reads prose (text, PDF, Markdown). This adds **tables** — CSV/TSV/PSV out of the box, any other format through a `RecordLoaderStrategy` — as a first-class source, without an LLM call per row, and so that a row and the passage that names the same thing land on **one node**.

```python
rag = GraphRAG(..., ontology=Ontology(tables=[
    TableMapping(source="employees.csv", label="Person", key="employee_id", name="full_name",
                 properties={"age": Column("age", "INTEGER"), "title": "job_title"},
                 links=[Link("WORKS_AT", to="Organization", by="org_id")]),
]))
await rag.ingest("employees.csv")     # rows → typed Person nodes + RELATES{rel_type:"WORKS_AT"}
await rag.ingest("acme_report.pdf")   # "Alice Smith" in the prose → the same Person node
await rag.finalize()
```

Docs: `docs/structured-ingestion.mdx` (guide), `docs/api-reference.mdx` § *Structured Ingestion*. Example: `examples/11_structured_ingestion.py`. CHANGELOG *Unreleased* has the full list.

## API surface

- `graphrag_sdk.core.tables`: `TableMapping`, `Column`, `Link`, `MappingError`. Mappings live on `Ontology.tables` and are looked up by the source's basename — `ingest()`/`update()` take no `mapping=`.
- `ingest(path)` routes `.csv/.tsv/.psv/.tab` to the record path (`loader=TextLoader()` opts out); returns `StructuredIngestionResult` (`records`, `rows_skipped`, `entities_created/updated/deleted`, `references_ambiguous`, …). `record_loader=` accepts any `RecordLoaderStrategy` (Parquet, a database cursor, in-memory rows); `strict_mapping=` refuses unmapped columns. `ingest(path, document_id="employees.csv")` re-syncs a table from a renamed export.
- `update(path)` re-syncs a table to its new export (rows added, changed, **removed**); `delete_document(table)` and new `drop_table()` take the table's columns back off every node while a document's own facts stay.
- A table with no `TableMapping` is not refused: when an LLM is configured the model proposes one from the header, a sample and the existing labels (deterministic `natural_mapping` otherwise). The proposal is stored `derived=True`, reported by `finalize().proposed_mappings` until a declaration replaces it, and every key/type it picks is checked against the data. `finalize()` also reports `probable_duplicates` it declined to merge and why, and `property_conflicts` with how many entities two tables actually disagree on.

## Design (method A, "shared node")

- **Identity.** A row's node id is `compute_entity_id(name, label)` — the same function prose extraction uses — so the two meet at write time, no merge pass. The key derives the id only when the row has no name column or the names are ambiguous.
- **Ownership.** Every column a table writes is signed with the table's namespace (`employees__age`), and the table's key is kept as `entity_key`; `is_stub` marks placeholders raised by a `Link` to a row not yet seen. Prose nev

title: [PR] Deduplication: finalize-time deduplicator fixes — ghost nodes, kept descriptions, name normalisation, acronyms
description:
## Deduplication — finalize-time deduplicator fixes

Measured on an 11-document benchmark against a real FalkorDB. Part of FalkorDB/research#88. First of five stacked PRs replacing #317.

### 1. Merging created empty ghost nodes
**Problem:** the edge-remap Cypher used a path-`MERGE` with an unbound survivor `(s {id})`, which creates a nameless `__Entity__` stub for every edge the survivor did not already have — 136 stubs from 24 merges on a 445-entity graph. The remapped edges hung off the stubs until `finalize()`'s NULL cleanup deleted them, losing the facts.
**Fix:** the survivor is `MATCH`ed before every `MERGE`; RELATES remaps union `source_chunk_ids` instead of overwriting. 0 stubs.

### 2. The absorbed entity's description died with it
**Problem:** only the survivor's description was kept.
**Fix:** descriptions are joined with `" | "` and the absorbed names recorded in `aliases`.

### 3. Name grouping was too loose in some places and too strict in others
**Fix:** normalisation folds accents, punctuation and inner dots (`A.I.` → `AI`) and strips only a leading **English** article (`Los Angeles` and `Le Mans` stay intact); generational suffixes are kept (`Elias Whitford, Jr.` ≠ `Elias Whitford`). An acronym joins its long form when exactly one same-label candidate spells it (`AIHS` / `Ashford Island Historical Society`); an ambiguous one (`US`) is left alone. Names in a non-Latin script no longer fold to `""` and merge with each other.

### 4. Fuzzy threshold 0.90 → 0.95
**Problem:** at 0.90 the name-embedding tier merged 2 of 33 deliberate hard-negative pairs for no added recall.
**Fix:** 0.95 in `EntityDeduplicator` and `deduplicate_entities()`.

### 5. "Index already exists" logged as ERROR
**Problem:** `ensure_indices()` re-creates indexes idempotently; FalkorDB answers with a non-transient error, surfaced as 5 ERROR lines per `finalize()`.
**Fix:** recognised and logged at DEBUG; every other non-transient failure keeps ERROR.

### Verification
Full suite: **1148 passed, 41 skipped**; ruff clean.

title: [Issue] Unguarded lazy init: concurrent requests redundantly load and re-register the ontology
description:
## Summary

`GraphRAG._ensure_ontology_initialized()` and `_validate_graph_config()` are unguarded lazy-init blocks. Both are awaited on every read path, and neither is protected against concurrent entry, so a burst of concurrent requests against a freshly constructed `GraphRAG` instance all run the full init — including ontology **writes** — instead of one request initializing and the rest reusing the result.

This surfaced while investigating a user report of retrieval throughput on a single graph looking serialized under load.

## Details

`_ensure_ontology_initialized()` (`graphrag_sdk/src/graphrag_sdk/api/main.py:387`) is a check-then-act on a plain bool:

```python
if self._ontology_initialized:
    return
loaded = await self._ontology_store.load()
if self.ontology.entities or self.ontology.relations:
    self._global_ontology = await self._ontology_store.register(self.ontology)
...
self._ontology_initialized = True
```

The flag is only set after several awaits, so every task that enters before the first one finishes passes the guard. Per redundant entry that is:

- 5 sequential read queries in `OntologyStore.load()` (`storage/ontology_store.py:136`), plus
- a full `OntologyStore.register()` pass when a user ontology was supplied — which **writes** to the `<graph>__ontology` graph.

FalkorDB takes an exclusive per-graph lock for writes, so N concurrent cold requests serialize against each other on redundant registration of an ontology that is already correct. The writes are idempotent, so this is a performance and contention bug, not a correctness one.

`_validate_graph_config()` (`api/main.py:2888`) has the same shape, guarded by `self._config_validated`. Its cost per redundant entry is a config query plus a live embedder probe (`aembed_query("dim_check")`), i.e. a billable provider round trip per in-flight request until one completes.

Both are reached from `retrieve()` (`api/main.py:2638-2639`) and `completion()` (`api/main.py:2784`), so this is on the hot path for every query, not just ingest.

## Reproduction

```python
rag = GraphRAG(connection=cfg, llm=llm, embedder=embedder, ontology=my_ontology)
await asyncio.gather(*[rag.retrieve("q") for _ in range(50)])
```

Expected: one ontology load + register, one embedder probe.
Actual: up to 50 of each. Observable as 50x `OntologyStore.load()` query volume against the `__ontology` graph, 50 embedder calls, and write-lock contention on the first burst.

## Suggested fix

An `asyncio.Lock` per instance with a double-checked flag inside:

```python
async with self._init_lock:
    if self._ontology_initialized:
        return
    ...
```

Same for `_validate_graph_config()` (separate lock, or one shared init lock). Notes:

- The lock must be created lazily or in `__init__` without binding a loop — `asyncio.Lock()` is loop-agnostic on 3.10+, so `__init__` is fine.
- `get_ontology()` deliberately re-reads after `_ensure_ontology_initialized()` to pick up other writers; that behavior should be p Labels: bug

description:
## Extraction — alternative NER backends (opt-in)

Part of FalkorDB/research#88. Stacked on #321. New API surface only; nothing changes unless you construct these.

### 1. `SpacyExtractor`
A second `EntityExtractor` backed by spaCy's NER (PERSON / ORG / GPE / LOC / FAC → Person / Organization / Location). Fast (~4 s for the corpus), offline. Requires `graphrag-sdk[spacy]` and a spaCy model.

### 2. `CompositeExtractor`
Chains extractors: the first one's entities win where spans overlap, later ones fill gaps. Built for GLiNER-first, spaCy-fills-in: the GLiNER default misses names like *Paris Observatory* and *Constantinople*; spaCy recovers 18 of those 24. Measured entity F1 0.568 → 0.609 at +0 s, answer accuracy unchanged — hence opt-in.

### 3. Exports
`SpacyExtractor`, `CompositeExtractor` and `DEFAULT_RELATION_TYPES` are importable from `graphrag_sdk` directly.

title: [PR] Extraction: default relation vocabulary and no early stop in relation extraction
description:
## Extraction — a default relation vocabulary, and no more early stop

Part of FalkorDB/research#88. Stacked on #320. Both changes are to the one step-2 prompt (entities + relations per chunk).

### 1. `DEFAULT_RELATION_TYPES`
**Problem:** entities always had a default ontology; relations had none — the prompt said "invent a descriptive label", so the same relation got a different name in every chunk. 447 distinct relation labels on the benchmark, only 17 % matching the answer key's 30; exact triple F1 0.065.
**Fix:** a 31-label default vocabulary offered to the LLM, the exact counterpart of `entity_types` — guidance, not a filter (labels outside the list are kept; `relation_types=[]` restores open vocabulary; a declared ontology overrides it). Vocabulary 447 → ~94, exact triple F1 2×; better on 5 of 5 unseen domains.

### 2. The relation extractor no longer stops early
**Problem:** the model treats the task as a summary — ~12 relations per chunk, then stops, using 2.5k of a 16k reply budget. Giving it twice the text grew the reply 1.3 %.
**Fix:** three prompt sentences ("exhaustive extraction, not a summary; there is no maximum; never end the list early"). +15 % relations for +4 % ingest time, and the best exact score of every variant tried — a second "what did you miss?" call gave more relations at 4.7× the time and a worse score, and is not in this PR.

### Verification
Full suite: **1179 passed, 41 skipped**; ruff clean.

title: [PR] Extraction: GLiNER windows over long chunks, per-model thresholds, 'Unknown' band
description:
## Extraction — GLiNER reads the whole chunk, per-model thresholds, "Unknown" band

Part of FalkorDB/research#88. Stacked on #319.

### 1. GLiNER reads the whole chunk
**Problem:** GLiNER truncates input at `config.max_len` silently — for `gliner_medium-v2.1` a probe entity at word 388 is always found, at word 389 never. Everything past that in a chunk was invisible; disabling the fix on the benchmark drops ceiling recall 0.805 → 0.621.
**Fix:** text longer than the window is processed as overlapping windows (overlap 48 word-tokens, above the model's 12-word `max_width`) and merged. Short text takes the old fast path.

### 2. Per-model confidence thresholds
**Problem:** one hard-coded 0.75 for every model. Scores are not comparable across models — the bi-encoders return 2 entities for a whole corpus at 0.75.
**Fix:** `DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS` (medium / large / medium-v2.5: 0.75; bi-small / bi-base: 0.50); `threshold=None` looks the model up, unknown models fall back to 0.5 with a warning. Default model stays `urchade/gliner_medium-v2.1` (bi-small measured better in August but returns 0 entities under gliner 0.2.27 / transformers 5.6).

### 3. "Unknown" band 25 % below the threshold
**Problem:** everything under the cutoff was discarded inside GLiNER; borderline real names were lost.
**Fix:** `candidate_threshold` defaults to `threshold × 0.75` (0.5625–0.75 for the default model). Spans in that band reach the step-2 LLM labelled `Unknown`, which re-types or drops them against the text; below the band is still discarded. `candidate_threshold=None` turns it off.
**Measured** (same code, band off vs on): NER spans 1,828 → 2,468; 0 `Unknown` nodes reached the graph (the LLM typed every kept one); entity recall 0.535 → 0.571 at precision 0.605 → 0.572 (F1 0.568 → 0.572); triple relaxed F1 0.228 → 0.236; answer accuracy 30.4 → 32.4 %; +8 % ingest cost. A wide fixed floor of 0.30 tested earlier was net negative (F1 −0.027), which is why the band is relative and narrow.
*Measured on `2e133d4`, which merged cross-window spans with the original label-scoped rule. Review rounds 1–2 (`40993b2`, `133a079`) replaced that merge — containment now loses to the container regardless of label, partial overlaps resolve by score — which changes which spans reach step 2, so these figures have not been re-measured against the current merge.*

### Verification

title: [PR] Extraction: dates, acronyms, junk tokens and reserved labels — entity-name hygiene
description:
## Extraction — entity-name hygiene

Part of FalkorDB/research#88. Stacked on #318. Four cases where a non-entity became a graph node, or a real entity was thrown away, all fixed in code (`is_valid_entity_name` / `_reject_reserved_labels`) rather than by asking the LLM.

### 1. Specific dates are not entities
**Problem:** "1896", "14 January 1904", "1003 CE" became nodes (23 % of the junk that reached the graph).
**Fix:** `is_specific_date()` rejects them as entity names when the ontology has no `Date` type; periods ("1820s", "19th century") are kept, and trailing sentence punctuation ("1823.") does not get a date past the gate. **Precondition:** `DEFAULT_ENTITY_TYPES` declares `Date`, so on the out-of-the-box path the rule never fires and the numbers above (23 % of junk, precision 0.577 → 0.642) apply only to a custom ontology that omits `Date`. Extractors receive the label list without an ontology (`entity_types=None` means "no date rule"); `GraphExtraction._step1` applies the gate once the ontology is known, so grounded discovery's NER anchor labels do not drop "1984" or "747".

### 2. `US`, `UN`, `EU` were dropped as pronouns
**Problem:** the stop-word filter lower-cased first, so `US` matched `us`.
**Fix:** a 2–3 letter all-caps token is read as an acronym and is exempted from the *pronoun* rows of the stop-list only; lower-case `us` is still removed, and `CD`, `ETC`, `MAN` in an all-caps heading are still rejected as the shell tokens and generic nouns they are. Residual: other all-caps pronouns (`HE`, `WE`, `MY`) pass, since they cannot be told apart from `US`/`IT` without context.

### 3. Junk tokens filtered in code
**Problem:** `+=`, `->`, `cd`, `he`, `they` reached the graph whenever the LLM ignored the prompt line asking it to drop them.
**Fix:** a hard rule in `is_valid_entity_name` (operators, shell abbreviations, generic 1–2 char tokens), in addition to the prompt line. Tests now assert behaviour, not prompt wording.

### 4. `Document` and `Chunk` rejected as entity types
**Problem:** the store uses those labels for its own nodes; an entity typed `Document` was stored as a file, invisible to dedup and retrieval (11 files uploaded → graph reported 106 documents).
**Fix:** `RESERVED_NODE_LABELS = {"Document", "Chunk"}`, the single definition shared by `GraphStore`, the Cypher generator and `reject_reserved_labels`. The match is **exact** (like the store's own membership test and FalkorDB labels), so `document` is allowed. The primary guard is in `OntologyStore.register`, before anything is persisted; discovery's `_validate_proposal` returns it as a retryable error so the LLM can pick another label; `backfill_entity` and `GraphExtraction.__init__`/`extract()` keep the check as defence-in-depth. The message names the clashing label.

### Verification
Full suite: **1210 passed, 41 skipped**; `ruff check src` and `ruff format --check src` clean. Note CI does not run on this PR (`ci.yml` triggers on `main`/`staging` only), so the stack's m

title: [PR] Extraction: share one GLiNER model, drop the inference lock, index ids, report failed chunks
description:
## Extraction — GLiNER speed & memory, and failed chunks reported

Measured on an 11-document benchmark against a real FalkorDB. Part of FalkorDB/research#88. First of five stacked PRs that replace #310.

### 1. One GLiNER model per process
**Problem:** every document being ingested loaded its own copy of the GLiNER model — 6 documents in one call = 6 models = 2.4 GB; 30 documents ≈ 11.6 GB.
**Fix:** a class-level cache keyed by model name; one copy shared by every document (+0 MB per document; 30 documents = 1.4 GB).

### 2. Inference lock removed
**Problem:** a lock around `predict_entities` serialised the chunks of a document even though they were dispatched to threads.
**Fix:** lock removed. GLiNER inference mutates no model state (verified: 8 documents in parallel vs serial, 5 trials, 40/40 identical). 1.56× faster NER.

### 3. Index on `id` per entity label
**Problem:** `MERGE` on `id` with no index scans every node — writes went from 4.6 ms to 2,195 ms per 500 entities as the graph grew to 50k nodes (477×).
**Fix:** `GraphStore` creates a range index on `id` for each label once, before its first write. Flat: 8.8 → 8.5 ms; 50k nodes 111 s → 0.69 s.

### 4. Failed chunks are reported
**Problem:** a chunk whose LLM call failed (timeout, bad JSON) contributed nothing and `ingest()` still reported success — an empty document and a broken run looked identical.
**Fix:** `GraphData` / `IngestionResult` carry `chunks_attempted` and `failed_chunks` (the ids, retryable) and a warning is logged.

### Verification
Full suite: **1126 passed, 41 skipped**; ruff check + format clean.

title: [PR] Chunking: idempotent re-ingest and a measured 384-token default
description:
## Chunking — three fixes

Measured on an 11-document benchmark against a real FalkorDB. Part of FalkorDB/research#88.

### 1. Re-uploading a file duplicated its chunks
**Problem:** every ingest gave chunks fresh random ids, so `MERGE` never matched — 17 → 34 → 51 chunks over three uploads of the same file.
**Fix:** chunk id is derived from document id + position + text (`_assign_deterministic_chunk_uids`). Same chunk → same id → stored once. 17 → 17 → 17. `ContextualChunking` hashes the original chunk text, not the LLM-enriched one.

### 2. Default chunk size 512 → 384 tokens
**Problem:** 512 was an unmeasured default; quality falls as chunks grow (relation F1 0.233 / 0.221 / 0.204 at 384 / 768 / 1536).
**Fix:** 384 in `SentenceTokenCapChunking`, `StructuralChunking`, `ContextualChunking`, the `CallableChunking` example, the `GraphRAG` docstring and the docs. Entity F1 0.574 vs 0.563, relation F1 0.237 vs 0.223 against 768. **Cost:** ~35 % more extraction LLM calls, ~19 % more input tokens per ingest (stated in the CHANGELOG). Re-measured on top of #310's prompt with the full stack, 3 repeats, against main with its LLM resolver on: exact relation F1 0.062 → 0.134, answer accuracy 27.0 → 32.0 %, QA input tokens −18 %, for +$0.03 per run.

### 3. Re-uploading an unchanged file still ran the whole pipeline
**Problem:** fix 1 kept the chunk count flat, but chunking, NER, the LLM calls and the graph writes still ran — 33 provider calls and ~30 s per re-upload, relations grew (105 → 121 → 129) and existing edge types were rewritten.
**Fix:** right after load, hash the document text and compare with the stored `Document` node's `content_hash`. Same hash → return before chunking with `IngestionResult.metadata.skipped_unchanged=True`, `chunks_indexed=0`. Measured: 0 calls, 0.01 s, 0 new chunks / entities / relations. The hash is written only after a run completes, so a partially failed ingest is retried in full. A changed file still takes the full path.

### Review follow-up (d38cf36)
- Fixes 1 and 3 now work for direct `IngestionPipeline.run()` too, not only via `GraphRAG.ingest()`: when no `document_info` is given the pipeline derives the Document id from the normalised source path (text mode: a text hash), mirroring `GraphRAG._resolve_document_id`. `update()` passes an explicit id and is unaffected.
- Unchanged-document check moved before chunking; `chunks_indexed` reports 0.
- `content_hash` written after steps 8/9, not in step 3.
- Dead `uid=sc.uid` in `structural_chunking.py` removed; docs updated to 384; CHANGELOG covers both fixes, the 384 cost, the one-time extra chunk copy on first re-ingest after upgrade, and edited-file re-ids.
- New tests: two `run()`s of the same file → same chunk ids (no `document_info`); same text in two files does not collide; text mode stable; chunker not called on skip; skip fires with a path-derived id; no hash after a failed extraction; contextual `original_chunk` hashing.

### Verification
Full suite on this branch:

title: [PR] fix: require falkordb>=1.7 so redis 8.1 installs are not broken
description:
Replaces #295, which GitHub locked after a force-push and won't reopen.

## Problem

Fresh installs failed on the first query:

```
TypeError: Redis.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'himport_registry'
→ DatabaseUnavailableError
```

`ping()` still returned `True`, so health checks passed and only real work broke.

## Cause

`falkordb`'s cluster probe copied `connection_kwargs` off the async pool and forwarded them to the sync `redis.Redis()` constructor, which rejects the pool-internal keys redis 8.1 added. falkordb 1.5.0 had also dropped its `redis<8.0.0` ceiling, so pip walked forward into 8.1.0.

## Fix

Fixed upstream in **falkordb 1.7.0** (filters the kwargs, bounds `redis<8.2`). This PR is the one-line consequence: `falkordb>=1.0,<2` → `falkordb>=1.7,<2`.

The bump is what makes the upstream fix guaranteed rather than incidental — `>=1.0` still allowed 1.6.x, which declares an unbounded `redis>=7.1.0` and can resolve against the broken redis. A fresh install happens to pick 1.7.0, but a lockfile or explicit `falkordb==1.6.x` reintroduces the bug.

`redis` is not declared here: falkordb owns it, and 1.7 bounds it to `>=7.2,<8.2`.

## Verification

Live FalkorDB, connect → create → query → delete:

| redis | falkordb 1.6.2 | falkordb 1.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| 8.1.0 | ✗ TypeError | ✓ |
| 8.0.1 | ✓ | ✓ |
| 7.4.1 | ✓ | ✓ |
| 7.2.0 | ✓ | ✓ |

Full suite on falkordb 1.7.0 + redis 8.1.0: 1096 passed, 40 skipped. No source changes, no new tests.

## Follow-ups (separate)

- `python-dotenv` is a core dep with zero imports anywhere; `docs/getting-started.md:60` tells users to load `.env` themselves.
- `transformers` is imported (`coref_resolvers.py:100`) but declared nowhere, relying on `gliner`/`fastcoref` — same shape as this bug, though guarded with a working fallback.

title: [PR] docs: structured data ingestion design proposal
description:
Design proposal for structured data ingestion. **Docs only — no SDK code.**

Refs: [FalkorDB/research#82](https://github.com/FalkorDB/research/issues/82) (POC) · design from [research#65](https://github.com/FalkorDB/research/issues/65) · supersedes #74

## The problem

`rag.ingest(...)` assumes prose. Structured inputs break three of its assumptions at once: the schema is already known, row identity is explicit, and typed columns shouldn't be re-discovered by an LLM. Today a mixed corpus needs a bespoke loader per format or pre-flattening to text, which throws away the structure that made the source valuable.

The design has to serve differently-shaped CSVs, nested JSON, a table lifted out of a PDF, and an existing graph that may or may not have its own ontology — all landing in one connected, traversable graph.

## The design

Reduce every structured source to a **stream of flat records**, and let **one declarative mapping** turn records into typed nodes and `RELATES` edges. Three ideas carry it:

1. **One intermediate representation** (`RecordBatch`). A PDF table becomes a record stream carrying the PDF's `DocumentInfo`, so its rows are chunks of the *same* `Document` as the prose. An existing graph becomes two streams — nodes and edges — because a graph is a node table plus an edge table. Neither is a special case any more.
2. **The mapping *is* an ontology fragment.** `mapping.to_ontology()` → validate / merge / bootstrap / reject. That single fact is the whole answer to "the existing graph may or may not have an ontology."
3. **Identity is declared once on the entity type**, not per source (`Entity(identity=["name"])`). A PDF mention of `Acme Corp` and a CSV row with `org_name="Acme Corp"` compute the *same* id and MERGE onto the *same* node — connected at write time, no similarity threshold, no LLM. A deterministic `AliasMatchResolution` bridges types keyed by a real business key (`sku`), since extraction can only ever produce a name.

Supporting decision with the most leverage: **a record is persisted as a `Chunk`** in the normal lexical graph. That inherits `update()`/`delete_document()` orphan cleanup, chunk retrieval over rows, and Zero-Loss provenance for free.

The result: **not one retrieval strategy changes.** Entity search, edge-fact search, chunk search, neighbour expansion and text-to-Cypher already see structured data. The doc includes a table justifying that claim path by path.

## Design review findings

The two central claims were walked against the code before publishing. Both hold, and the walk surfaced three requirements and one gap — all folded into the document:

- Structured writes **must** set `name` on nodes and `fact` **and** `source_chunk_ids` on `RELATES` edges. Omitting any one silently breaks entity embedding, edge embedding, or stale-edge GC respectively.
- **Correctness trap:** record chunk uids must key on the *run's* effective document uid, never the canonical id. `update()` runs against `pending_id = f"{reso

title: [PR] Resolution and dedup: LLM-verified default, unified candidate stage, finalize-time fixes
description:
## Summary

Reworks entity resolution and finalize-time deduplication. Every default here was measured against a real FalkorDB and a real LLM on the benchmark gold set (216 duplicate pairs, 39 must-not-merge pairs); numbers are in the commit messages and CHANGELOG.

## Commits

1. **refactor(resolution)** — remove `SemanticResolution` and `DescriptionMergeResolution`. Neither was reachable from production code; both were strictly weaker than `LLMVerifiedResolution`.
2. **feat(resolution)** — `LLMVerifiedResolution`: unified same/cross-label candidate stage (`unified_threshold=0.65`, `soft_threshold` 0.80→0.65: +26 % recall, 0 extra wrong merges), batched verification on by default (5 pairs/call, 4000-token budget — larger batches were bimodal on identical input), `merged_labels` recorded on cross-label merges, `flatten_remap` for merge chains. `ExactMatchResolution` now matches on `name` (was `id`, which never merged anything).
3. **feat(storage)** — `merged_labels` promoted to real Cypher labels on write (a property is not a type: `MATCH (n:Engineer)` missed nodes that had absorbed `Engineer`). Structural labels are never promoted.
4. **fix(dedup)** — `EntityDeduplicator`: survivor is `MATCH`ed before every `MERGE` (path-MERGE created 136 NULL-name stubs from 24 merges), `source_chunk_ids` unioned, absorbed descriptions kept, safer name normalisation (`A.I.`→`AI`, foreign articles kept), acronym fold with same-label and ambiguity guards (`US` matching two long forms is left alone). Grouping stays `(name, label)`.
5. **feat(api)** — `ingest()`/`update()` default resolver is `LLMVerifiedResolution`; pass `resolver=ExactMatchResolution()` for a zero-cost ingest. Fuzzy dedup threshold 0.9→0.95 (0.90 merged 2 of 33 hard negatives for no recall).

title: [PR] Extraction: entity and relation quality, memory and throughput fixes
description:
## Extraction — entities and relations

Every claim below was measured on an 11-document benchmark corpus against a real
FalkorDB, not estimated. Part of the ingestion investigation in FalkorDB/research#88.

18 commits, one per fix, each verified by running the code before it was committed.

---

# Entities

### Updated / fixed

- **The name-finding model default changed** — `urchade/gliner_medium-v2.1` →
  `knowledgator/gliner-bi-small-v2.0`. Ceiling recall 0.805 vs 0.709, 432MB vs 781MB on
  disk, 1004MB vs 1532MB resident, ~14s vs ~29s, 2048-word window vs 384. Smaller,
  faster, finds more.
- **The confidence cutoff was one hardcoded number applied to every model** — now a
  per-model table with a sane fallback and a warning, so swapping models can't silently
  mis-tune the threshold. That single number was the actual cause of a 4-second spaCy
  model appearing to beat our shipped config: the bi-encoder models return **2 entities
  for an entire corpus** at the 0.75 that suits the old model, and raise nothing.
- **The name-finder silently ignored everything past word 388 of a chunk.** No exception,
  no warning — the tail never reached the model. It now slides overlapping windows across
  the whole chunk and merges the results; without it recall drops 0.805 → 0.621. Spans
  are re-offset into the original text so downstream span code stays correct.
- **Specific dates like "January 5, 1992" were stored as things in the graph** — 63 of 274
  false entities (23%). Now rejected by name. Precision 0.577 → 0.642, recall unchanged.
  Periods ("the 1820s", "the Abbasid era") deliberately stay.
- **`US` the country was thrown away as `us` the pronoun** — the stoplist check casefolded
  first. Short all-caps tokens are now read as acronyms.
- **Junk tokens (shell fragments, pronouns, operators) were only filtered by asking the
  LLM nicely** — they're now a hard rule in code as a backstop. A prompt instruction can
  be quietly skipped; a list cannot.
- **Every upload loaded its own copy of the model** (~395MB each, ~11.6GB for 30
  documents) — one shared process-wide cache now, ~1.39GB.
- **A lock forced name-finding one chunk at a time despite the model being safe in
  parallel** — inference now takes no lock at all, **1.56×** faster. (#71 claimed 3.44×;
  the honest measured figure is 1.56×, because torch already uses the cores.) Thread
  safety was tested, not assumed: 40/40 documents byte-identical to the serialised run.
- **New `SpacyExtractor`** — a second, different name-finder, added and exported.
- **New `CompositeExtractor`** — runs several finders and merges overlapping spans, added
  and exported.
- **An entity type named `Document` collided with our own bookkeeping and vanished from
  search** — 106 documents reported in an 11-document corpus, *and* the node never got
  `__Entity__` so it silently dropped out of dedup and retrieval. Now rejected up front on
  both the `entity_types` and ontology paths, and the spaCy mapping that caused it

title: [Issue] [Feature] Add Agno as an optional multi-provider LLM backend with end-to-end observability
description:
## Use Case

GraphRAG-SDK currently supports LLM access through providers such as LiteLLM, OpenRouter, and custom implementations of `LLMInterface`.

It would be useful to support [[Agno](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno)](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno) as another optional LLM backend. The developer should remain free to choose how GraphRAG-SDK accesses language models:

```text
GraphRAG-SDK
└── LLMInterface
    ├── LiteLLM
    ├── OpenRouterLLM
    ├── AgnoLLM
    │   └── Agent
    │       └── Any Agno model provider
    └── Custom provider
```

The goal is not to replace the existing providers or make Agno mandatory.

When `AgnoLLM` is selected, all LLM calls performed by GraphRAG-SDK should be executed through a reusable Agno `Agent`. This includes calls made during:

- Entity and relationship extraction
- Entity resolution and deduplication
- Ontology discovery and evolution
- Attribute and relationship backfilling
- Question rewriting
- Text-to-Cypher generation
- Answer generation

Routing these calls through Agno would provide centralized observability and make it possible to capture:

- Input, output, and total tokens
- Reasoning tokens
- Cache read and write tokens
- Model and provider information
- Latency and time to first token
- Errors, retries, and fallback behavior
- Run, agent, session, and request identifiers
- Estimated cost when pricing information is available
- Trace correlation for each GraphRAG pipeline stage

This is particularly valuable for regulated, auditable, explainable, and cost-sensitive applications.

Agno supports multiple native providers, cloud platforms, local runtimes, and model gateways. Therefore, the integration must not be tied to OpenAI or any other specific provider.

## Proposed Solution

Add an optional adapter implementing GraphRAG-SDK's existing `LLMInterface`:

```python
from graphrag_sdk.integrations.agno import AgnoLLM
```

The adapter should receive a reusable Agno `Agent`, following Agno's standard public API:

```python
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.anthropic import Claude
from graphrag_sdk import GraphRAG
from graphrag_sdk.integrations.agno import AgnoLLM

agno_agent = Agent(
    name="graphrag-llm",
    model=Claude(id="claude-sonnet-4-5"),
    instructions=(
        "Execute GraphRAG pipeline tasks accurately. "
        "Return only the requested output."
    ),
    markdown=False,
)

rag = GraphRAG(
    connection=connection,
    llm=AgnoLLM(agent=agno_agent),
    embedder=embedder,
)
```

Changing providers should only require changing the model configured on the Agno Agent:

```python
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.openai import OpenAIResponses

agno_agent = Agent(
    name="graphrag-llm",
    model=OpenAIResponses(id="gpt-5.4"),
    markdown=False,
)

rag = GraphRAG(
    connection=connection,
    llm=AgnoLLM(agent=agno_agent),
    embedder=embedder,
)
```

The same integration should work with any compatible Agno model provider, including Anthropic, Op Labels: enhancement

comments.author: razdgann
comments.text:
The pipeline stage metadata is especially valuable here. Aggregate token totals alone will not tell you whether extraction, entity resolution, rewriting, or answer generation is responsible for the cost.

I would keep a provider neutral request ID at the adapter boundary and preserve both estimated cost at request time and provider reported usage. That makes it possible to compare pipeline stages and later reconcile the traces against the provider invoice.

comments.author: homerokzam
comments.text:
Thank you for the suggestion — I found it very interesting, and I completely agree. Combining a provider-neutral request ID with pipeline-stage metadata, estimated cost, and provider-reported usage would make the traces much more useful for cost analysis and invoice reconciliation.

More broadly, I believe a pluggable, framework-neutral integration layer could become an important capability for GraphRAG-SDK. Beyond providing access to additional models, agent frameworks can contribute native tracing, token and cost accounting, retries and fallbacks, evaluations, guardrails, tool execution, session management, and human-in-the-loop workflows.

Agno could be the first reference adapter, while the same integration pattern could support future community adapters for:

- [[Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/)](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/)
- [[LangChain and LangGraph](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview)](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview)
- [[Hugging Face smolagents](https://huggingface.co/docs/smolagents/main/index)](https://huggingface.co/docs/smolagents/main/index)

Each adapter could preserve access to its framework’s model ecosystem—OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Groq, OpenRouter, Hugging Face Inference, Ollama, and local models—without adding provider-specific behavior to the GraphRAG-SDK core.

I would keep this issue focused on Agno while designing the adapter boundary as a reusable integration pattern rather than a one-off implementation.

title: [PR] Add "Reducing LLM Hallucinations" docs page and cross-link it from core docs
description:
Publishes a permanent, directly-linkable docs page explaining how GraphRAG SDK reduces unsupported LLM answers through grounded retrieval, source provenance, and abstention — and cross-links it from the highest-traffic existing pages.

## New page

- `docs/reducing-llm-hallucinations.mdx`, slug fixed at `reducing-llm-hallucinations` (`https://docs.falkordb.com/graphrag/reducing-llm-hallucinations`)
- Opens verbatim with the required framing paragraph; no H1 in body (Mintlify renders `title`)
- Maps each grounding mechanism to the real `MultiPathRetrieval` pipeline: vector search, full-text/keyword search, graph traversal + relationship expansion, ontology-guided text-to-Cypher (off by default), cosine reranking
- Shows how `MENTIONED_IN` edges trace answers back to source chunks, with a verified `completion(..., return_context=True)` snippet
- Includes a copy-pasteable `answer_or_abstain()` helper that checks retrieval evidence before returning an answer
- Covers ontology as an extraction guardrail and how to spot-check grounding
- Closes with an explicit caveat that benchmark accuracy is not a hallucination-rate guarantee

```python
async def answer_or_abstain(rag, question: str, *, min_evidence_items: int = 1) -> str:
    result = await rag.completion(question, return_context=True)
    evidence_count = sum(
        1 for item in (result.retriever_result.items if result.retriever_result else [])
        if item.metadata.get("section") in ("passages", "facts", "cypher_results", "relationships")
    )
    if evidence_count < min_evidence_items:
        return "I don't have enough supporting evidence in the knowledge graph to answer this confidently."
    return result.answer
```

## Navigation & cross-links

- Registered the page in `docs/docs.json` (Home group, after `architecture`)
- Linked prominently from `docs/index.mdx` (entry card), `docs/architecture.mdx` (near `MENTIONED_IN`/provenance), `docs/retrieval.mdx` (multi-path intro), and `docs/benchmark.mdx` (top + caveats, framing the score as a ceiling)
- Added rows/bullets to `README.md` and `graphrag_sdk/README.md` documentation lists

## Out of scope for this repo

Two of the six requested link sources live outside this repository and are not addressed here — flagging for a maintainer with access to those properties:

- **GraphRAG landing page** (graphrag.falkordb.com / falkordb.com marketing site): add a link with anchor text "Reducing LLM hallucinations" → `https://docs.falkordb.com/graphrag/reducing-llm-hallucinations`

title: [PR] docs: add Reliability and Grounding page
description:
The docs describe how the pipeline works, but never in the vocabulary evaluators use to judge whether a RAG framework produces trustworthy, citable answers — searches for "grounded retrieval", "source provenance", "abstention" return nothing, even though the underlying capabilities exist under implementation-specific names.

Adds `docs/reliability-and-grounding.mdx`, mapping each of those terms onto a real class, parameter or returned field. Every claim was checked against `api/main.py`, `retrieval/strategies/`, `storage/` and `ingestion/pipeline.py` before writing.

### Page structure

- **Vocabulary map** — term → implementing API, up front so the page is scannable.
- **Grounded retrieval** — `completion()` retrieval-then-generation, the `</context>` neutralisation and delimited system prompt, and the warning that a custom `prompt_template` opts out of both.
- **Source provenance** — the `Document ─PART_OF→ Chunk ←MENTIONED_IN─ __Entity__ ─RELATES→` chain, per-node field tables, `RELATES.source_chunk_ids`, the `[Source: <path>]` passage prefix, and `document_id` as a stable citation key.
- **Evidence trail** — walking `RagResult.retriever_result.items` and `item.metadata["section"]`, plus Cypher for chunk → document and entity → passages.
- **Relationship-aware retrieval** — the six `MultiPathRetrieval` paths and its real constructor defaults.
- **Confidence thresholds** — full cutoff table (`min_score=0.25`, `max_facts=12`, `min_keep=3`, `chunk_top_k=15`, `top_k=5`, …) and a note that scores are now similarities where higher is closer.
- **Unsupported claims**, **Retrieval validation**, **Factual accuracy** — `return_context=True` verification, `retrieve()` as a no-LLM diagnostic, and what ACC/ROUGE-L/Cov/FS measure.

### Where the SDK does not implement a concept, the page says so

- **Abstention** is prompt-level only — no confidence field on `RagResult`, no threshold that rejects a generation. The page states this and shows the supported gate:

```python
retrieved = await rag.retrieve(question, reranker=CosineReranker(embedder=embedder, top_k=10))
strong = [item for item in retrieved.items if (item.score or 0.0) >= MIN_SCORE]

if len(strong) < MIN_ITEMS:
    answer = "I don't have enough information in the knowledge base to answer that."
else:
    answer = (await rag.completion(question, return_context=True)).answer
```

- **Metadata filtering** has no `filter=` parameter. Loader metadata is flattened onto `Document`/`Chunk` properties, so the documented approaches are Cypher and per-scope `graph_name` isolation.
- **Scores** are `None` on `MultiPathRetrieval` section items unless a `CosineReranker` is attached — called out so the threshold examples above aren't misread.

### Two deliberate divergences from the issue text

- Uses `MENTIONED_IN`, the actual relationship type, not `MENTIONS`.
- Examples construct `GraphStore(connection)` rather than `rag.graph_store`; other pages use the latter, but the attribute is private (`_graph_store`) —

title: [PR] docs: add standalone GraphRAG accuracy benchmark citation page
description:
The benchmark proof already existed as a README blockquote and a methodology-focused `docs/benchmark.mdx`, neither of which works as a landing target for someone searching "is GraphRAG more accurate than vector RAG?". This repackages that data into a standalone, self-contained page a reader (or an LLM) can cite without clicking through, while keeping `benchmark.mdx` as the deep reference.

### New page — `docs/graphrag-accuracy-benchmark.mdx`

Title: *GraphRAG Accuracy Benchmark: FalkorDB vs Vector RAG for Reliable LLM Answers*.

- **Above the fold:** 71.48 vs 55.39 comparison table with per-dataset split (Novel 66.09 vs 48.35, Medical 76.87 vs 62.43) and an explicit delta row (+17.74 / +14.44 / **+16.09**, ~29% relative).
- **Evidence:** dataset/question counts, per-category ACC tables for both subsets, full model + embedding config, and the two declared deviations from SDK defaults (`enable_cypher=True`, `embedding_dimension=1024`) with justifications.
- **Definitions:** the ACC and Overall formulas, plus the judge settings (`gpt-4o-mini`, `bge-large-en-v1.5`, temp 0, seed 42) as a standalone table.
- **Reproduction:** four-step `<AccordionGroup>` (install → datasets → published ontologies → index/answer/judge) and the measured indexing costs. Runner + pinned deps stated plainly as available on request, with issue and Discord links.
- **Limitations:** competitor numbers not re-run, the `Novel-55f0c0e2` duplicate id, evaluator skips (2,053/2,062 and 1,995/2,009), judge variance, two-domain generalization, and that Overall is our own average.
- **"What a benchmark does and does not tell you":** benchmark = task performance on a fixed dataset; production hallucination reduction additionally needs source-data quality, retrieval scoping, prompting, and abstention logic. Framed as *score raises the ceiling, system determines the floor* — deliberately worded as reduce/ground/verifiable, never "eliminates".
- **How to cite:** plain-text line and BibTeX, both stamped August 2026 / SDK 1.3.0.

### Wiring

- Registered in `docs/docs.json` under `Reference`, ahead of `benchmark`.
- `docs/benchmark.mdx` gains a `<Note>` pointing at the new page; the new page links back to it as the methodology reference.
- Root `README.md`: the benchmark blockquote's "see the benchmark page" now lands on the comparison page, retaining the methodology link alongside it; new row in the Documentation table. Matching entry added to `graphrag_sdk/README.md`.

### Number provenance

Every figure is copied verbatim from `docs/benchmark.mdx` or the root `README.md`. The only derived values are the three deltas and the ~29% relative figure, computed from those published numbers. No figures were unverifiable.

One MDX gotcha worth noting for reviewers: bare autolinks (`<https://…>`) fail the MDX compile because `<` parses as JSX — links in the resources table use standard markdown link syntax instead.

title: [PR] fix(retrieval): one LLM repair round for rejected text-to-Cypher queries
description:
Fixes #292 (repair round + remaining fail-fast classification).

## What

Text-to-Cypher queries that pass the safety allowlist but get rejected by FalkorDB currently degrade silently: `execute_cypher_retrieval` catches the execution error and returns empty results, and the two error classes from the benchmark runs in #292 that are not in `_NON_TRANSIENT_MARKERS` still burn the full 3-attempt retry budget on identical input.

1. **One repair round** — when execution fails, `execute_cypher_retrieval` now sends the failed query plus the FalkorDB error back to the LLM for exactly one corrected attempt (`_repair_cypher`). The repaired query must pass the same `validate_cypher` read-only allowlist as a fresh generation, so the repair path cannot smuggle in writes. If the repaired query also fails, the path degrades to empty results exactly as before — no retry loop.
2. **Fail-fast for the remaining deterministic errors** — `_NON_TRANSIENT_MARKERS` now also covers the two error classes observed in #292 that were not classified yet: alias-reused-for-node-and-relationship and unexpected-clause.

The optional observability suggestion from #292 (surfacing per-path failure stats) is not included here.

## Why

Per #292's benchmark runs, 1.5–2.9% of generated queries failed deterministically; every failure cost a full 3x retry on identical bytes (90–177 wasted round trips per run) plus a 100% recall loss on those questions, because no repair was ever attempted. FalkorDB's errors are specific enough that one LLM repair round should recover most of them.

## How I verified

New tests in `graphrag_sdk/tests/test_cypher_generation.py` (mock LLM + mock graph store, no live services):

- repair round is attempted exactly once with the server error included in the prompt, and a successful repair produces results
- a repair that fails again returns empty results with no retry loop (exactly 2 executions)
- a "repaired" write query is blocked by `validate_cypher` and never reaches the database
- the two newly classified error strings (plus the previously covered ones) are non-transient, while connection errors remain transient

The existing suite is unchanged — the silent-degradation test now exercises the repair path and still returns empty results.

No change to the success path: generation and first execution behave identically, and the repair only activates after a failure, so benchmark accuracy is unaffected by construction. Happy to run the 100-question benchmark if maintainers want the numbers.

title: [PR] fix(deps): raise dependency floors to patched versions for Dependabot alerts
description:
## Summary

Reviewed all 127 open Dependabot alerts on the repo. **Every alert is filed against `uv.lock` at the repository root — a file that no longer exists** (it was removed in the v2.0 rewrite, which moved the project to `graphrag_sdk/pyproject.toml` with no lock file). Those alerts are stale and should auto-close on Dependabot's next scan of `main`.

The genuinely actionable issue is that `graphrag_sdk/pyproject.toml` declares dependency *floors* that are below the patched versions, so a fresh `pip install graphrag-sdk[...]` with an old resolver or a pre-existing environment can still land on a vulnerable release. This PR raises those floors.

## Changes

`graphrag_sdk/pyproject.toml`:

| Package | Before | After | Advisories addressed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `python-dotenv` (core) | `>=1.0` | `>=1.2.2` | Symlink following in `set_key` allows arbitrary file overwrite (medium) |
| `pypdf` (`pdf`, `all`) | `>=6.9.2` | `>=6.15.0` | 31 alerts — infinite loops on unterminated inline images (high ×2), memory exhaustion via XMP/form XObjects/`/ToUnicode`/CID width ranges, ignored stream-length limits |
| `litellm` (`litellm`, `all`) | `>=1.83.0` | `>=1.84.0` | Auth bypass via Host header injection (critical), MCP auth bypass via OAuth2 passthrough (high), `/user/update` self-role escalation (high), API-key route escalation (high), path traversal in Skills archive extraction, OIDC local file read |
| `pytest` (`dev`) | `>=8.0` | `>=9.0.3` | Vulnerable tmpdir handling (medium) |

Transitive-only packages with alerts (`aiohttp`, `requests`, `urllib3`, `idna`, `protobuf`, `setuptools`, `pyasn1`) were deliberately **not** pinned — over-constraining transitive deps in a library hurts downstream consumers. Verified that current resolution already picks patched versions of all of them (see Testing). The `jupyterlab` / `jupyter-server` / `notebook` / `nbconvert` / `mistune` / `bleach` / `tornado` / `soupsieve` / `Pygments` alerts came from notebook tooling in the deleted lock file and have no counterpart in the current manifest.

## Testing

- `uv pip compile --python-version 3.10 pyproject.toml --extra all --extra dev` resolves cleanly. Resulting versions include `aiohttp==3.14.3`, `urllib3==2.7.0`, `idna==3.19`, `requests==2.34.2`, `protobuf==7.36.0`, `pypdf==6.16.1`, `litellm==1.97.0`, `python-dotenv==1.2.3` — all at or above their patched versions.
- `pip install -e ".[dev]"` in a clean Python 3.12 venv, then `pytest tests/ -q`: **1096 passed, 41 skipped**. No breakage from the pytest 8 → 9 jump.
- `pytest>=9.0.3` requires Python >=3.10, which matches the project's `requires-python = ">=3.10"`, so the 3.10/3.11/3.12 CI matrix is unaffected.

## Memory / Performance Impact

N/A — dependency metadata only, no code changes.

## Related Issues

Addresses the actionable subset of https://github.com/FalkorDB/GraphRAG-SDK/security/dependabot

title: [Issue] Vector search returns least-similar results first (ORDER BY score DESC on a distance)
description:
## Summary

`VectorStore.search_chunks`, `search_entities` and `search_relationships` order results with `ORDER BY score DESC`, but FalkorDB's vector index returns **distance** (0 = identical), not similarity. The result sets are therefore returned **worst match first**.

`storage/vector_store.py`, lines ~362, ~396, ~446.

## Reproduction

Query the chunk index with a chunk's own embedding. It must come back first at distance 0:

```python
v = (await rag.embedder.aembed_documents([paragraph_text]))[0]
res = await rag._vector_store.search_chunks(v, top_k=3)
```

Observed on SDK 1.3.0:

```
[1] score=0.4652  'Bryan Namoff (born May 28, 1979 in Carson City...'   <- unrelated
[2] score=0.4554  'The Montreal Impact () is a Canadian professional...'  <- unrelated
[3] score=0.0000  'Erik Hort (born February 16, 1987 in Montebello...'   <- the exact paragraph
```

The exact self-match scores 0.0000 and is ranked **last**.

After changing `DESC` to `ASC` in those three queries:

```
[1] score=0.0000  'Erik Hort (born February 16, 1987 in Montebello...'   <- correct
[2] score=0.4554  'The Montreal Impact...'
[3] score=0.4652  'Bryan Namoff...'
```

## Corroboration inside the same file

`search_relationships` contains both orderings — `ORDER BY dist ASC LIMIT $top_k` in one query and `ORDER BY score DESC` in another. The ascending form is the intended one.

`fulltext_search_chunks` / `fulltext_search_entities` (lines ~519, ~562) correctly keep `DESC`, since fulltext relevance is higher-is-better. Only the three vector methods are affected.

## Impact

Measured on multi-hop passage retrieval (MuSiQue, 1000 questions, `bge-large-en-v1.5`, pooled corpus of 9,838 paragraphs), using the vector path alone:

| | Recall@2 | Recall@5 | Recall@10 | Recall@15 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Vector search as shipped | 3.25 | 5.83 | 14.25 | 58.58 |

Gold passages are present in the returned set but sorted to the bottom — the signature of inverted ordering.

`MultiPathRetrieval` partially masks this because `CosineReranker` re-sorts afterwards, but the damage happens earlier: candidate selection pulls in the *worst* vector matches, so the reranker never sees the best ones. On the same benchmark, MultiPath's pool recall caps at 64–77% because the correct passages were never candidates.

Anyone calling `search_chunks` / `search_entities` directly gets worst-first results with no mitigation.

## Fix

`ORDER BY score DESC` -> `ORDER BY score ASC` in the three vector-index queries (`search_chunks`, `search_entities`, `search_relationships`). Leave the two fulltext queries as they are.

Worth adding a regression test that queries the index with a stored vector and asserts it comes back at rank 1 — that catches this class of bug directly.

comments.author: galshubeli
comments.text:
**Correcting the impact section above.** The bug is real and the fix is right, but I overstated its effect on `MultiPathRetrieval`.

Measured after applying `ORDER BY score ASC`, same graph and embedder, MuSiQue (100 questions):

| | Recall@2 | Recall@5 | Recall@10 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Vector search, as shipped | 3.25 | 5.83 | 14.25 |
| Vector search, fixed | **29.67** | **44.33** | **52.75** |
| MultiPathRetrieval, as shipped | 35.42 | 50.92 | 61.42 |
| MultiPathRetrieval, fixed | 35.42 | 50.92 | 61.42 |

So:

- **Direct callers of `search_chunks` / `search_entities` are badly affected** — Recall@5 rises from 5.83 to 44.33 with the fix. That is the real severity of this issue.
- **`MultiPathRetrieval` is essentially unaffected.** It gathers 66–83 candidates across four paths and `CosineReranker` re-sorts the whole pool, so the vector path's internal ordering rarely changes the final selection. On a 1000-question rerun, 998 of 1000 retrieved lists were byte-identical before and after the fix.

My earlier claim that this explains MultiPath's pool-recall ceiling was wrong — that ceiling has a different cause and I'll investigate separately rather than attribute it here.

The fix is still worth making: the ordering is incorrect, and the public API returns worst-first results to anyone using it directly.

title: [PR] fix: order vector node searches by distance
description:
## Issue

Closes #294.

## Background

FalkorDB vector-index scores are distances, where lower values are closer matches. The node and relationship vector search paths previously exposed some results in descending order, returning less similar results first to direct callers.

## Changes

- Order chunk, entity, and relationship vector-index searches by ascending distance.
- Keep the relationship fallback ordered by ascending cosine distance.
- Add multi-row regression coverage with an exact `0.0` self-match for all three search methods.
- Document that returned `score` values represent distances.

## Compatibility

This changes only the ordering of direct vector search results so the closest matches are returned first. Public method signatures and result shapes are unchanged.

title: [Issue] Migrate docs to mintlify
[PR] fix: require falkordb>=1.7 so redis 8.1 installs are not broken
description:
## Problem

Fresh installs failed on the first query:

```
TypeError: Redis.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'himport_registry'
→ DatabaseUnavailableError
```

`ping()` still returned `True`, so health checks passed and only real work broke.

## Cause

`falkordb`'s cluster probe copied `connection_kwargs` off the async pool and forwarded them to the sync `redis.Redis()` constructor, which rejects the pool-internal keys redis 8.1 added. falkordb 1.5.0 had also dropped its `redis<8.0.0` ceiling, so pip walked forward into 8.1.0.

## Fix

Fixed upstream in **falkordb 1.7.0** (filters the kwargs, bounds `redis<8.2`). This PR is the one-line consequence: `falkordb>=1.0,<2` → `falkordb>=1.7,<2`.

The bump is what makes the upstream fix guaranteed rather than incidental — `>=1.0` still allowed 1.6.x, which declares an unbounded `redis>=7.1.0` and can resolve against the broken redis. A fresh install happens to pick 1.7.0, but a lockfile or explicit `falkordb==1.6.x` reintroduces the bug.

`redis` is not declared here: falkordb owns it, and 1.7 bounds it to `>=7.2,<8.2`.

## Verification

Live FalkorDB, connect → create → query → delete:

| redis | falkordb 1.6.2 | falkordb 1.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| 8.1.0 | ✗ TypeError | ✓ |
| 8.0.1 | ✓ | ✓ |
| 7.4.1 | ✓ | ✓ |
| 7.2.0 | ✓ | ✓ |

Full suite on falkordb 1.7.0 + redis 8.1.0: **1096 passed, 40 skipped**. No source changes, no new tests.

## Follow-ups (separate)

- `python-dotenv` is a core dep with zero imports anywhere; `docs/getting-started.md:60` tells users to load `.env` themselves.
- `transformers` is imported (`coref_resolvers.py:100`) but declared nowhere, relying on `gliner`/`fastcoref` — same shape as this bug, though guarded with a working fallback.

description:
GitHub serves [default community health files](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file) from the org-wide [`FalkorDB/.github`](https://github.com/FalkorDB/.github) repository to every repo that does not define its own. This repo's Code of Conduct is a 12-line pointer that contains no policy text of its own, so this PR removes it and lets the org-wide version apply.

## Removed

- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — it links out to the Contributor Covenant and names a reporting address, with no policy text of its own. The org-wide file contains the full Covenant text inline, so a reader no longer has to follow a link off GitHub to find out what the terms actually are.

## Two behaviour changes worth noting

Please confirm you're happy with both, as they are not purely cosmetic:

1. **Reporting contact:** `support@falkordb.com` → `info@falkordb.com`, which is the address used by the org-wide policy and by every other repo in the org. If `support@` is deliberately the intended CoC channel for this repo, say so and I'll adjust the org-wide file instead of changing it here.
2. **Cited Covenant version: resolved.** This originally said the org-wide file was v2.0, one version behind this repo's citation. The org-wide file has since been bumped to **v2.1** in [FalkorDB/.github#3](https://github.com/FalkorDB/.github/pull/3), so once that merges the version cited here is unchanged by this PR.

   Correcting something this PR said earlier: the 2.0 → 2.1 delta is *only* the pledge adding "caste, color". An earlier revision of this description claimed enforcement was also reworded; a diff against the canonical upstream text shows Standards, Scope, Enforcement and the Enforcement Guidelines are byte-identical between the two versions.

## Also in this PR

Both `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` contained a relative link, `[Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)`, which would have 404'd once the file was gone. Both now point at the org-wide file's URL.

## Deliberately left alone

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — has real repo-specific content (dev setup, build and test commands, code style), which the org-wide default cannot replace.
- `SECURITY.md` — defines a scope that explicitly excludes the FalkorDB server and third-party LLM providers, and adds SDK-specific guidance on API keys and Cypher injection. Genuinely repo-specific, so it stays and continues to override the org default.

## Effect

The Code of Conduct still shows up in this repo's Community Standards page and in the issue and PR sidebar; it is just served from the org repo now. Note that default files are not included in clones or release tarballs of this repository.

title: [Issue] Text-to-Cypher: invalid generated queries are retried 3x and never repaired
description:
## Summary

`validate_cypher()` ([`retrieval/strategies/cypher_generation.py:347`](https://github.com/FalkorDB/GraphRAG-SDK/blob/main/graphrag_sdk/retrieval/strategies/cypher_generation.py#L347)) is a **safety allowlist, not a syntax check**. It verifies the query starts with a read-only keyword, contains a `RETURN`, has no writes / `CALL` / `LOAD CSV`, and references only known labels. Nothing validates Cypher grammar.

Syntactically invalid generated queries therefore pass validation and fail inside FalkorDB at execution time:

```
Invalid input 'F': expected OR or OPTIONAL MATCH
The alias 'r' was specified for both a node and a relationship
Unexpected clause following RETURN
```

## Observed

GraphRAG-Bench Medical, 2062 questions, `gpt-4o-mini`, `enable_cypher=True`, SDK 1.3.0:

| Run | Failed Cypher queries | Rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 59 | 2.9% |
| 2 | 30 | 1.5% |

Each failure is logged as `FalkorDB query failed after 3 attempts: ResponseError`.

## Two problems

**1. Deterministic errors are retried 3x.** A syntactically malformed query cannot succeed on retry — the input is identical each time. That is 90–177 wasted round trips per run, on the critical path of a user's question.

**2. No repair attempt.** The FalkorDB error message is specific and actionable (`Unexpected clause following RETURN`). Feeding it back to the LLM for a single repair pass would recover most of these. Today the Cypher path silently contributes nothing for those questions.

## Impact

Latency and lost recall, not correctness. `MultiPathRetrieval`'s other paths cover the gap — both benchmark runs produced complete answers with 0 errors and 0 empty answers — which is exactly why this is invisible in normal use.

Note this is on the experimental path (`enable_cypher` defaults to `False`), but it is enabled in the configuration behind our published [GraphRAG-Bench results](https://github.com/FalkorDB/GraphRAG-SDK/blob/main/docs/benchmark.md), so it is running in a configuration we support and advertise.

## Suggested fixes

1. Do not retry on `ResponseError` where the message indicates a syntax/semantic error — fail fast instead. Cheap, removes ~2/3 of the waste immediately.
2. On a syntax failure, send the query plus the FalkorDB error back to the LLM for one repair attempt before giving up.
3. Optionally, count and surface Cypher-path failures in retrieval metadata so the rate is observable rather than log-only.

title: [PR] feat: chunk-level extraction cache for update() (cache_unchanged_chunks)
description:
## What

Two changes, both aimed at making `update()` cheap and reliable.

**1. Chunk-level extraction cache** (opt-in: `cache_unchanged_chunks=True`)

A chunk whose text is byte-identical (SHA-256) to one already stored for the same document **skips LLM extraction entirely**. Its entities, relationships and mentions are rebuilt from the live graph and remapped onto the new chunk uids.

Editing one paragraph of a 50-chunk document now costs ~1 extraction instead of 50.

This extends the existing document-level no-op short-circuit down to chunk granularity, reusing the `extractor=` hook `update()` already exposes. No new `update()` function — the existing one gains a flag.

**2. Fix: config validation rejected provider-prefixed model names**

`EmbedderConfig.to_embedder()` builds `azure/text-embedding-3-large` when a provider is set, but the name stored on the graph is unprefixed. `_validate_graph_config` compared the two raw strings — so pointing an existing graph at a provider (same model, same dimensions) raised `ConfigError` and broke **every** update from then on.

Both sides are now normalized before comparing: a leading `<provider>/` is stripped when the prefix is a known litellm provider. The check itself stays — a genuine model swap silently corrupts vector search, since old and new embeddings are never comparable and nothing ever raises.

## How

- **`CachedChunkExtraction`** (new, exported) — a decorator `ExtractionStrategy`. The graph is the cache; nothing extra is stored.
- **3 new `GraphStore` read accessors** + `ChunkEntityRow` / `ChunkRelationshipRow` — schema coupling stays in the storage layer.
- **`cache_unchanged_chunks: bool = False`** on `update()`, `update_sync()`, `apply_changes()`, `apply_changes_sync()`. Stats land in `UpdateResult.metadata["cache_stats"]`.
- **`_bare_model_name()`** — provider list read from litellm once and cached, with a static fallback.

## Safety

- Cache reads happen in Phase 3, while the old chunks still exist (they're deleted at the Phase 5 cutover). The crash-safe pending/commit/rollforward state machine is untouched.
- Deterministic entity ids MERGE onto existing nodes (`SET n +=` preserves embeddings). `source_chunk_ids` remap: own old ids → new uid(s) or dropped; other documents' ids pass through. RELATES provenance is UNIONed.
- Re-emitted mentions keep entities alive through scoped orphan cleanup. Duplicate identical chunks each get their own provenance. Label-less entities skip the node write (MERGE would mint a duplicate) but keep the mention.
- **Fail-open**: any cache lookup or rebuild error falls back to full extraction. Worst case is LLM spend, never data loss.

## Caveats (also on the docstring + CHANGELOG)

- The graph is the cache, so manually deleted entities are **not** resurrected from unchanged chunks.
- Ontology / prompt / model changes do **not** re-extract cached chunks.
- Defaults to `False`; existing behavior is byte-identical until you opt in.

## Testing

**1056 passed, 0

comments.text:
Ran the suite on this branch: 166 passed, 12 skipped. Design holds up, and confirmed there's no duplicate update path — `update()` just gained a flag.

**1. `CachedChunkExtraction` is exported but only safe inside `update()` — Medium**

It never checks that the doc id it reads differs from the one the pipeline is writing chunks to. That only holds today because `update()` writes under a pending node while the cache reads `resolved_id`. If they ever coincide (wired into `ingest()`, or the pending indirection changes), `get_document_chunk_texts()` returns old *and* new rows with identical text, `setdefault` picks whichever came back first, and a chunk can map to itself → no MENTIONED_IN rows → counted as cached, skips the extractor, entities silently dropped. Fail-open can't catch it (no exception) and `cache_stats` still looks fine. The unit tests miss it because `FakeGraphStore` returns an old-only list.

Fix is ~3 lines: skip any returned id in `{c.uid for c in chunks.chunks}`.

**2. `get_relationships_for_chunks` scans every RELATES edge — Medium (perf)**
`any(c IN r.source_chunk_ids WHERE c IN $cids)` isn't index-servable, so cost scales with total graph size, not document size. Won't show at 19 chunks. Start the scan from the entity set you already have.

**3. Duplicate accessor — Low**
`get_document_chunk_texts` and `get_document_chunk_ids` are the same traversal, one extra column, and both run in the same `update()` call. Pass the existing `old_chunk_ids` snapshot in instead.

Approve once #1 is addressed; #2/#3 are fine as follow-ups.

title: [PR] docs: update GraphRAG-Bench results and correct averaging method
description:
Updates the published GraphRAG-Bench figures to a full August 2026 run across **both** subsets, and fixes an averaging inconsistency in the previous numbers.

## Results

| | Novel | Medical | Overall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Was | 63.73 | 75.73 | 69.73 |
| Now | **66.09** | **76.87** | **71.48** |

## Why the old Novel figure was not comparable

The previous **63.73** was the *question-weighted* average of the four task categories. The GraphRAG-Bench leaderboard — and therefore every competitor number printed beside it — uses the *unweighted mean* of the four.

Computed the leaderboard's way, that same run scored **62.62** on Novel, not 63.73. This mattered for the headline claim:

| Formula | FalkorDB | vs AutoPrunedRetriever 63.72 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Question-weighted (as published) | 63.73 | +0.01 |
| Unweighted mean (leaderboard's) | 62.62 | −1.10 |

The new run leads on both subsets under the leaderboard's own formula, so no composite is needed to make the claim. Both equations are now stated explicitly under the README table.

Verified: every competitor's Overall in the table reproduces exactly from `(Novel + Medical) / 2`. Only our own row used a different method.

## Configuration behind the new numbers

`gpt-4o-mini` (Azure OpenAI) at temperature 0.7 for both graph construction and generation, GraphRAG-SDK 1.3.0 on FalkorDB, `text-embedding-3-large` at 1024 dimensions, text-to-Cypher enabled, scored with the benchmark's own `Evaluation/generation_eval.py` **unmodified**.

Two settings sit above the SDK defaults and are declared as such in `docs/benchmark.md`: `enable_cypher=True` (default `False`) and `embedding_dimension=1024` (default `256`). Both are single global values chosen before any results were scored and applied identically to both subsets.

## Ontologies are published

Both hand-authored ontologies are checked in at `docs/benchmark/`. They are the artifact behind the corpus-only claim, so publishing them lets that claim be verified without the runner — the files contain domain type definitions only, with no question, answer or evidence text.

The reproduction package itself (runner, ontology builders, pinned dependencies) is available on request via Issues or Discord rather than published.

## Corrected claims

Several places attributed **84.8%** to "the 20-document novel benchmark." That figure is from `docs/retrieval.md` — an internal ablation over 100 questions scored 0–10 by an LLM judge, a different corpus, scale and metric. The example carrying the claim (`03_custom_strategies.py`) also uses GLiNER2 NER, `DescriptionMergeResolution` and `FixedSizeChunking`, none of which produced the benchmark results. The number and the "benchmark-winning" framing are removed rather than replaced, since no GraphRAG-Bench run used that configuration.

That example also only composes *ingestion* strategies — it never passes `retrieval_strategy` — so its description is corrected accordingly in the docstring and both READMEs.

title: [Issue] Resolution: same-name / different-type entities never merge (homograph gap)
description:
## Problem
When the extractor assigns an entity **different types** across chunks/documents, it splits into multiple nodes that never merge. All three dedup checkpoints key on `(name, label)`, so a same-name/different-type duplicate falls through every one:

1. per-document resolver — groups by `(name, label)`
2. write `MERGE (n {id})` — id is `name__type`, so different type = different id
3. `finalize()` `EntityDeduplicator` — groups by `(normalized_name, label)`

## Evidence
In the docs graph, `GraphRAG` exists as two nodes: `graphrag__concept` and `graphrag__technology`.

Impact on answers — asking **"What is GraphRAG?"**:
- Fragmented graph: *"GraphRAG is a chat feature in Code-Graph…"* (narrow/incorrect — last-writer-wins description)
- Graph where the two nodes are merged: *"GraphRAG is a graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation technique…"* (correct)

Same retrieval budget, materially better answer purely from resolving the entity.

## Root cause
`compute_entity_id(name, type)` keys identity on `name+type`, and `EntityDeduplicator` groups by `(normalized_name, label)` — so cross-type homographs are never compared.

## Proposed fix
Add a same-name / cross-type pass to the global `finalize()` dedup: group by **normalized name**, and merge when descriptions are similar (free, embedding-based) while **preserving genuine homographs** (e.g. Paris the city vs the person) when descriptions diverge. LLM only for ambiguous cases.

title: [PR] feat(resolution): IncrementalResolution — graph-aware entity linking
description:
New `IncrementalResolution` strategy + exports, and it is wired as the **default resolver** in the `GraphRAG` facade.

**Behavior change:** when an LLM and embedder are configured, ingestion now defaults to `IncrementalResolution` (was `ExactMatchResolution`), which adds LLM + embedding calls per ingest. It falls back to `ExactMatchResolution` automatically when no LLM/embedder is present, so LLM-free setups are unchanged; opt out explicitly with `resolver=ExactMatchResolution()`. Documented in `docs/ingestion.md`, `docs/strategies.md`, and CHANGELOG.

Closes #277

---

Closes #277

## What

Adds `IncrementalResolution`, a resolution strategy that resolves a document's
entities **against the knowledge graph built so far** — so a mention in today's
document can be linked to an entity extracted from a document ingested earlier.
Ordinary batch resolvers only deduplicate a document's entities among
themselves and structurally cannot see cross-document duplicates.

## Algorithm

A funnel — cheap, certain work first; the LLM only where cheap signals can't decide:

1. **collapse** — merge a batch's own same-name duplicates (description-gated, no LLM)
2. **retrieve** — for each survivor, fetch look-alike existing graph entities
3. **pile** — group survivors that share a candidate (union-find)
4. **link** — one LLM call per pile: which items are the same entity, and which
   existing node (if any) is the merge target

Two duplication axes, each handled where it's cheapest and most reliable:
- **same name, different type** (`GraphRAG` Concept vs Technology) → resolved for
  free by description similarity. An LLM told to be careful tends to *over-split*
  these; the embedding is cheaper and more accurate.
- **different name, same entity** (`llama_index` ≈ `LlamaIndex`, or a new mention
  of an existing node) → the LLM partitions a small pile, the framing that keeps
  genuine look-alikes apart (`FALKORDB_USERNAME` ≠ `FALKORDB_PASSWORD`).

## Design choices

- **Fail toward splitting** — thin evidence or a failed call leaves entities separate.
- **Existing nodes win the id** — the store's `MERGE (n {id})` attaches the new
  mention with no special-casing; existing edges untouched.
- **Facts are never invented** — the LLM owns free text (canonical name, type,
  merged description); provenance is unioned and immutable-property conflicts are
  flagged (`_needs_review`), never guessed.
- **Testable without a database** — the graph lookup is an injected
  `candidate_retriever`; in production it wraps the graph store's name/vector search.

## Scope
